articles.title: Shopify Drops React Native for Swift and Kotlin as AI Changes Cross-Platform Development Tradeoffs
articles.text:
Shopify recently announced it is abandoning React Native to rewrite its flagship apps in Swift and Kotlin. With the significant jump in the quality of AI models, Head of Mobile Mustafa Ali reassessed Shopify’s commitment to React Native, estimating that the benefit/cost ratio of maintaining native codebases across mobile platforms was now above that of using an abstraction layer.
The about-face shift comes after Shopify declared in 2020 that React Native was the future of its mobile architecture, reaffirming again in 2025 its commitment after a successful 5-year migration of all its apps to React Native.
The rationale then was three-fold: stop building the same features twice, talent portability, and spending more time delivering value to users vs. chasing feature parity. Shopify at the time reported increased development productivity with apps that were both blazing-fast (<500ms screen loads) and stable (>99.9% crash-free sessions). Reactive Native features such as hot reloading and TypeScript were also mentioned as notable productivity enablers.
Yet, even then, Shopify did not discard native platform development entirely:
Native is still the best way for building cutting-edge features that leverage device hardware like 2D / 3D scanning and running AI models on-device. It is also better suited for building features that have memory limitations like home and lock screen widgets, Apple Watch apps and complications, App Intents, and Siri Shortcuts.
Native is also the better choice for long-running background jobs.
Instead of thinking native or React Native, think native and React Native.
A little over a year later, Shopify has now reassessed its technological choices, driven in particular by two key factors. The first was a looming significant refactor to adopt React Native’s New Architecture:
That work would have required us to revisit native module integrations, rendering, and the boundaries between shared and platform-specific code
Shopify was thus faced with a major engineering effort that made a deeper analysis of engineering options worthwhile.
The second factor was the fast-paced improvement in quality of AI coding models, agents, and harnesses. After a successful proof of concept led by a single engineer in just one week, six engineers rebuilt the flagship Shop app from the ground up to production deployment in 12 weeks, further reinforcing the clean-slate greenfield rewrite option over a migration.
By standardizing on modern declarative UI frameworks—Apple’s SwiftUI and Google’s Jetpack Compose—the team leveraged structural and mental model symmetries between platforms to guide autonomous agents while matching platform-native idioms.
Shopify reports improvement in cold startup latency (dropping 23% on iOS and 50% on Android), session stability (from 99.5% to 99.95%, i,e, a 10x reduction in sessions that crash), 75% faster release build times on Android. Also on Android, native feed scrolling maintained sustained 120 FPS throughput without requiring extensive manual optimization.
(Native vs. React Native comparison on Android. Source: Migrating Shop app from React Native to native)
In spite of the progress in AI coding models, the rewrite did still require considerable engineering involvement in architecture, planning agent work, validating task completion and remediating errors. Developers are encouraged to read both published in-depth articles.
An interesting detail however is that Shopify isolated the factors of change (the mobile platform, the UI) from the core, stable business logic and application state management to mitigate the slow feedback loops inherent to mobile simulators. AI models would thus dispatch actions, manipulate navigation state, and assert outcomes in milliseconds, on the desktop, without rendering UI or using a simulator. Simulators are reserved primarily for automated end-to-end integration passes.
The announcement unsurprisingly led to extensive debate in the mobile development community. One argument is that Shopify’s reported performance and productivity results are measured vs. the old React Native architecture instead of the new one, leaving open the possibility that migrating to the new architecture may have achieved similar or better results. Another significant tradeoff reported by developers is the difficulty of over-the-air updates when going full Native. Shipping a new version of the app may require going through the app review process gate, thus slowing down release frequency. One developer wondered if this being perceived as a strong argument in favor of React Native is not influenced by a web culture that contrasts significantly with the native development ethos:
I’ve worked with both native and cross-platform. I think the mentality of being able to make changes quickly without much review often comes from cross-platform, especially when the developers come from a web background.
Changes are cheap and fast, so teams often feel less pressure to test everything thoroughly before a release. […]
With native, you know each release is harder to roll back, so you tend to build more tooling around releases, think through changes more carefully, and test more thoroughly before they’re ready to ship. You opt for one bigger, more stable release every few weeks instead.
At the end of the day, both approaches work.
Shopify plans to complete its Point of Sale, and Inbox apps over the coming year, with the Shopify app (with 300+ screens, home & lockscreen widgets, Apple Watch app, Siri Shortcuts) due to completion this year.

articles.title: AMD et Nvidia repousseraient le lancement de leurs futures cartes graphiques à 2028
articles.text:
L’information vient de Kepler_L2, un leaker suivi de près dans le petit monde du hardware PC, qui a lâché le calendrier sur les forums d’AnandTech. Le site spécialisé Wccftech l’a repérée et lui donne 70 % de crédibilité. Si le scénario se confirme, il faut le dire tout de suite : la plupart des joueurs vont garder leur carte actuelle encore plus d’un an avant de pouvoir vraiment passer à la génération suivante.
AMD ne sortirait rien en 2027 côté RDNA 5, sa future architecture graphique. Nvidia ferait pareil en décalant sa série RTX 60 (nom de code Rubin) à 2028, alors que d’autres rumeurs la donnaient pour début 2027. Rien d’officiel là-dedans : ce sont des sources internes et des bruits de couloir, à prendre avec des pincettes.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Quelles sont les meilleures cartes graphiques de 2026 ? Le comparatif et classement des RTX 50, RX 9000
            
Une seule carte sauverait 2027
L’exception s’appelle AT2. C’est une puce basée sur l’architecture RDNA 5 d’AMD, positionnée en milieu de gamme, avec 40 unités de calcul (les blocs qui font tourner les jeux). Ce serait la seule à sortir en boutique l’an prochain, pendant que tout le reste attendrait 2028.
Là où ça devient intéressant pour les joueurs : cette AT2 viserait le haut de gamme actuel de Nvidia, du niveau de la RTX 5080. Aujourd’hui, la meilleure carte d’AMD reste la RX 9070 XT, qui se bat plutôt contre la RTX 5070 Ti. Avec RDNA 5, AMD s’attaquerait enfin au segment premium qu’il avait laissé de côté avec la génération RDNA 4. Et il pourrait poser une carte musclée sur le marché avant même que Nvidia ne dégaine sa future gamme.
La pénurie de mémoire plombe tout
Ce report tient beaucoup à l’état du marché. La mémoire graphique manque, aspirée par la demande en intelligence artificielle, et ça fait grimper les prix des cartes : sur le début 2026, les RTX 50 et RX 9000 se paient environ 23 % au-dessus de leur tarif conseillé en Europe. Étrangement, cette flambée n’a pas fait fuir les acheteurs, puisque les ventes de cartes graphiques ont plutôt bien tenu.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Meilleure carte graphique AMD Radeon en 2026 : notre sélection
            
C’est la même pénurie qui aurait déjà eu la peau des RTX 50 SUPER. Ces versions boostées en mémoire de Nvidia semblent annulées : le fabricant avait déjà suspendu leur lancement à cause de la VRAM, et il sauterait carrément l’étape pour aller directement vers la famille Rubin. Pour l’acheteur qui lorgnait une carte d’entrée ou de milieu de gamme comme une RTX 5060, ça veut dire pas de vraie nouveauté avant un moment.
Si ce calendrier se vérifie, 2027 sera une année creuse pour qui veut changer de carte graphique, avec la seule AT2 d’AMD en nouveauté. Rien n’est confirmé par les deux constructeurs, et les leakers eux-mêmes rappellent que tout ça peut encore bouger. En attendant, les prix ne montrent aucun signe de baisse.

articles.title: Nvidia rejected an RMA over a fading serial number, and other RTX 5090 owners say they've seen it too
articles.text:
WTF?! Nvidia has rejected an RMA request for an RTX 5090 Founders Edition after determining that the card's serial number could not be read, according to a Reddit user. Other RTX 5090 owners have described similar fading on the markings, though the limited reports show different outcomes when cards are submitted for warranty service.
The owner said the GPU began suffering black-screen crashes and was sent to Nvidia for replacement. Before shipping the card, they noticed that the serial number printed on its metal bracket had become difficult to read.
Nvidia retained the flagship for more than a month before returning it, the owner said. The company did not initially explain why it rejected the RMA. After contacting support again on September 14, the user said Nvidia highlighted the unreadable serial number as the reason for the decision.
The Reddit post said the GPU had not been altered. The owner wrote that they had "never opened, modified, repaired, or tampered with the card."
The owner added that Nvidia's support chatbot said the claim could proceed if they had the original box and proof of purchase. Both were available, but Nvidia declined the replacement after receiving the hardware.
Several commenters on the post said they had seen the same kind of fading on Founders Edition cards. The serial number is printed in gray on a metal portion of the I/O bracket, where the text can become difficult to distinguish from the surrounding surface.
My RTX 5090 FE RMA was rejected because the physical serial number is no longer readable – has anyone experienced this?
by u/Willing-Avocado-4830 in nvidia
PC Gamer reported a similar issue with the serial number on its own RTX 5080 Founders Edition, which the publication said had faded, though it did not report sending that card in for warranty service or having an RMA rejected.
One Reddit commenter said the issue became apparent while trying to photograph the number: "When I went to take a photo of the serial number, I noticed it was faded almost the same color as the metal bracket it was printed on... It just seems designed in such a way to make it easy to refuse RMAs."
The reports do not establish how common the fading may be or what causes it. Some suggested that heat exposure or normal handling could be involved.
Comment
by u/Willing-Avocado-4830 from discussion
in nvidia
At least one commenter said Nvidia approved an RTX 5090 RMA despite a similarly faded number. That suggests other identifying records, including information on retail packaging or purchase documentation, may be considered in some cases.
The situation has raised plenty of questions about how Nvidia evaluates claims when physical identifiers deteriorate but customers can still provide original packaging and purchase records. It's especially concerning when the card in question now sells for anywhere from $7,000 to $10,000.

articles.text:
Harry Potter (HBO Max) : on sait quels acteurs seront Arthur Weasley, Mimi Geignarde et Colin Crivey
On sait désormais qui seront les interprètes d'Arthur Weasley, Mimi Geignarde et Colin Crivey dans la série Harry Potter attendue sur le service de streaming HBO Max.
Alors que la sortie de la série Harry Potter se rapproche à grand pas, HBO Max ne perd pas de temps et se lancera bientôt dans le tournage de la saison 2, adaptée du roman Harry Potter et la Chambre des Secrets. Pour se faire, trois nouveaux acteurs ont été recrutés pour des rôles clés.
Arthur Weasley, Mimi Geignarde et Colin Crivey entrent en scène
Trois nouveaux acteurs ont été choisis pour compléter le casting de la saison 2 de la série Harry Potter d'HBO Max. Rafe Spall (Trying) incarnera le rôle d'Arthur Weasley, papa de Ron (Alastair Stout) et Ginny (Bonnie Hill), Molly Hewitt-Richards (Casualty) jouera le rôle du fantôme Mimi Geignarde, et Jasper Ambrose (Les Moutons Détectives) prêtera ses traits au personnage de Colin Crivey, nouvel élève de la maison Gryffondor très heureux de rencontrer Harry Potter (Dominic McLaughlin).
Dans Harry Potter et la Chambre des Secrets, le "garçon qui a survécu" doit affronter une nouvelle menace à Poudlard alors que l'ouverture de la mystérieuse Chambre des Secrets met en danger les élèves de l'école de sorcellerie.
Pour Spall, Harry Potter est une affaire de famille puisque son père, Timothy Spall, est apparu dans la saga cinématographique adaptée des romans de JK Rowling dans le rôle de Peter Pettigrew/Queudver.
Ce trio rejoint ainsi les acteurs déjà sélectionnés pour la saison 2 d'Harry Potter, dont Kit Harington (Gilderoy Lockhart), Lenny Rush (Dobby) et Billy Barratt (Tom Jedusor).
La série Harry Potter est écrite et produite par Francesca Gardiner (Succession). Mark Mylod assure également la production exécutive et réalise plusieurs épisodes. Pour la saison 2, Gardiner partage le poste de showrunner avec Jon Brown (Succession).
Harry Potter à l'école des sorciers, la première saison de la série, arrivera sur HBO Max à Noël prochain.

articles.title: PlayStation dévoile deux nouveaux casques audio : le Pulse et le Pulse Edge
articles.text:
Près de deux ans après la sortie du Pulse Elite, Sony revient avec deux nouveaux casques audio sans fil destinés à la PS5 : le PlayStation Pulse et le PlayStation Pulse Edge. Le premier mise sur une qualité sonore et une spatialisation des sons de pointe, tandis que le second va encore plus loin avec des fonctionnalités supplémentaires et des transducteurs magnétiques planaires plus performants.
Tout savoir sur le PlayStation Pulse
Le casque PlayStation Pulse intègre des transducteurs magnétiques planaires « conçus sur mesure et inspirés des studios professionnels », avec quatre aimants par transducteur, qui permettent de mettre la membrane en mouvement grâce au champ magnétique généré. Sony assure que ces transducteurs offrent une spatialisation des sons « exceptionnelle », chose particulièrement importante lorsque l’on joue à un jeu vidéo, comme par exemple un FPS compétitif (bruit de pas, de tirs, etc.). Les micros intégrés au casque audio proposent quant à eux une réduction de bruit optimisée par l’IA, filtrant ainsi les bruits de fond. À noter que ce casque n’intègre pas de réduction de bruit active qui bloque les sons environnants.
Tout savoir sur le PlayStation Pulse Edge
Le Pulse Edge offre quant à lui des fonctionnalités supplémentaires par rapport au Pulse. Il intègre notamment des transducteurs magnétiques planaires dont le volume magnétique est deux fois supérieur à celui du PlayStation Pulse, avec par ailleurs huit aimants par transducteur (contre 4 pour le Pulse), ce qui permet des basses plus riches et profondes, tout en préservant la précision et la clarté qui permettent de percevoir des détails subtils. Et contrairement au Pulse, le Edge intègre une réduction de bruit active pour atténuer les bruits ambiants, un accès rapide au réglage de l’équilibre entre le son du jeu et le chat vocal sur PS5, une prise jack 3,5 mm, ainsi qu’un microphone détachable. Le Edge est par ailleurs fourni avec un étui de protection.
Que ce soit le Pulse ou le Edge, les deux casques bénéficient de transducteurs planaires plus larges, offrant des basses plus riches et plus profondes, par rapport au Pulse Elite sorti en 2024. Notons enfin que les deux casques sont compatibles avec la technologie PlayStation Link, qui promet un son sans perte avec une latence très faible. Cette technologie permet aussi de passer facilement d’un appareil compatible à l’autre, comme une PS5, un PlayStation Portal, un PC ou un Mac. Les casques peuvent également être connectés en Bluetooth à un autre appareil en parallèle.
Les deux casques seront proposés en blanc et en noir. Sony précise que le Pulse sera disponible « sur certains marchés dès les fêtes de fin d’année », tandis que le Edge sera lancé début 2027. Les prix de ces deux nouveaux produits sont pour l’instant inconnus.

articles.title: I’ve spent more than 200 hours playing Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave, and I can confidently say it’s the best game on Nintendo Switch 2 — here’s why
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is a masterful tactical RPG that beautifully combines an engrossing multi-path narrative, addictive turn-based combat, and enjoyable exploration. Dungeon sections help maintain excellent pacing throughout, and the sheer scale of the world means you can easily sink hundreds of hours into this experience without seeing everything. Pair that with solid visuals, a great cast of characters, and an amazing soundtrack, and you’re looking at one of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games released thus far.
Pros
- +Phenomenal turn-based combat with some fresh mechanics
- +Multi-path story offers hundreds of hours worth of content
- +Gripping storytelling and excellent dialogue throughout
- +Dungeon sections add some welcome variation
Cons
- -Support grind can feel a little repetitive
Why you can trust TechRadar
Every now and then, a game comes along that doesn’t just entertain and engage me — it totally enraptures me. It stands as a pure work of art that reminds me of exactly why I love this medium and captures the essence of a book you just can’t put down. For me, that’s exactly what Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is — an engrossing experience that I simply can’t get enough of.
Platform reviewed: Nintendo Switch 2
Available on: Nintendo Switch 2
Release date: September 17, 2026
This Nintendo Switch 2-exclusive tactical JRPG offers a combination of excellent turn-based combat and rewarding exploration, alongside captivating storytelling and a great cast of characters. And its sheer scale cannot be understated — I’ve spent north of 200 hours in Fortune’s Weave, and there’s still so much more I have to see.
I’ve played through each of the four Flame Lords’ paths and taken the battle to the demonic god Balor, and I’ve got a number of thoughts about gameplay, visuals, and narrative to share. So, without further ado, let’s take a look at why Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is one of the best Nintendo Switch 2 games you can play right now.
Four paths converge
I won’t get into the weeds of the premise in Fortune’s Weave, but to sum up, you’re able to play as four heroes, known as the Flame Lords, as they compete in a grand arena event known as the Heroic Games. The champion of the Games will be granted a wish of their choosing by Divine Sovereign, Solel, who rules over the land of Dagda and its capital, Dagsion.
After completing the brief prologue — which acts as a solid tutorial for newcomers — you can select any of the Flame Lords’ paths and play through them in any order you like from a central hub area. This approach works nicely, as you don’t have to replay the prologue each time you start a new journey, and you’re able to dip in and out of each story as you please.
This makes up Part I of the game, which was probably my favorite overall. Although some cutscenes and quests are the same across the four stories, they still feel distinct and gripping in their own right. Each pathway has a distinct tone and feeling to it, with each Flame Lord having a deeply personal ambition and a unique set of close allies. For instance, the vengeful and skilful Leda is joined by the womanizing bard Sirocco and protective warrior Buccar, whereas Dietrich is partnered with the excitable Esmeralda and bizarre and eccentric missionary, Fabio.
The core cast of characters is truly excellent, but you’ll also be able to recruit more allies as you progress the story, including foes you face in the Heroic Games and parties of interest across Dagsion. Many of these units can be recruited across all four stories, though their recruitment requirements often vary, which encouraged me to experiment with different characters across different stories.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Anything with Dietrich and Fabio. They're an unlikely yet incredible duo, with Dietrich's bloodlust and Fabio's eccentricity somehow combining to create some of the most hilarious — and sometimes emotive — dialogue in the series.
What makes the multi-path system click is that you’ll uncover revelations in one story that answer questions — or even pose new ones — about events in one of the other paths. There are plenty of twists and turns — some perhaps more obvious than others — which change the way you perceive certain characters and add substantial depth to units that may seem less significant on some paths than others.
This cross-path storytelling is done really well, and the narrative is strong, more generally. I won’t spoil anything, but it’s got its fair share of shock instances, touching moments, and character development that help it to hit — and if not, exceed — the standards that the series has set thus far.
Gameplay-wise, things are kept pretty fresh too. Each Flame Lord has specific abilities that they can make use of on the world map and beyond, with Dietrich able to battle warriors and learn their combat arts, Leda capable of holding performances to unlock unique materials, Theodora able to recruit warriors to assign battalions, and Cai skilled enough to wrangle mounts for himself and his allies.
And luckily, all of this comes together nicely in the latter parts of the game. While Part I is more individually tailored to each Flame Lord and their journey through the Heroic Games, paths begin to converge in Part II, known as the War Arc. Again, I won’t spoil anything here, but Part II offers far less variation across each pathway, but there are still some interesting differences in dialogue, and the way you approach battles will likely change considerably.
I loved how the enormity of Fortune’s Weave came together in Part III, though. Here, you’ll be able to unite all of the Flame Lords beside the game’s true protagonist, you. It’s awesome that you’re able to make use of all of the heroes’ unique abilities and even re-recruit old units for the final battle against the demonic lord, Balor.
Being able to bring all of your units, inventory, and abilities into a singular, epic finale is incredibly rewarding and makes building the ultimate army even more enjoyable.
I see grids in my sleep
Let’s delve a bit more deeply into gameplay, which, as you’d expect, is outstanding in Fortune’s Weave.
For the most part, you’ll be battling on classic grid-based battlefields. Honestly, I’ve fought on these so many times I’m starting to see them in my dreams. It's that classic turn-based Fire Emblem that you know and love, with some returning features, like Combat Arts (which provide benefits in exchange for weapon durability) and gambits (in Theodora’s path), for instance.
But there are new mechanics too, like Blaze Arts, which are unique to specific units. By sacrificing HP, Blaze Arts enable you to deal more damage, move further, buff allies, and more. The health trade-off means they don’t feel like a cheat code, and they also fill a blaze gauge, which will burst at a certain point, forcing you to work with reduced HP for the rest of the map.
Standard battles feel brilliantly balanced, and I never felt that difficulty spikes were too severe or that I had to grind much to push past my opponent. When you do want to grind, though, you can enter into a skirmish against foes on the world map, or try your luck in a dungeon.
Dungeons work a bit differently, and you’ll move around a 3D area to face foes in Clash Battles. These are a bit different and combine light action segments with more traditional turn-based JRPG combat rather than tactical grid-based battles. I think that they’re a great option if you want a break from the usual maps and want a faster-paced method for gaining experience or class proficiency for your units.
That’s not to say that the standard maps aren’t engaging though; quite the opposite. There’s some excellent map variety, and some battles will ask more of you than just routing the enemy. In some cases, I had to defeat more giants than my opponents, rescue defenseless citizens from a huge serpent, or even collect missing cargo before thieves made off with it. Battlefields are also delightfully diverse throughout the heroic games, and become even grander as the stakes rise towards the back end of the game.
If at any point you’re struggling, you can make use of Blessings, enabling you to rewind to a previous turn, increase your strength, or reduce the cost of Combat Arts, for example. I kept usage of these to a minimum, as I was playing on the slightly more gracious Normal/Casual difficulty. But there’s also a Hard mode, and you can play Classic (where units are permanently lost when they fall in battle), where Blessings will likely feel a bit more necessary.
All in all, combat is incredibly addictive, varied, and offers impressive depth. Building a squad with the right balance in terms of classes and weapons is massively satisfying, and breaking things up with a bit of dungeon crawling keeps the experience feeling fluid and fun for the game’s full runtime. And given that we’re talking about a title that will take you well over 100, if not 200, hours to finish, that’s an impressive feat in itself.
Beyond the battlefield
Before I wrap up, I want to touch on my experience with Fortune’s Weave outside of battle. There’s quite a bit to do, both within the capital, Dagsion, and in the land of Dagda more broadly.
Dagsion has all of the stuff you’d expect. A training ground to boost your aptitude with specific weapons, a shopping district, an inn for viewing support conversations and restoring motivation (which is used for training and increasing your Blessings level), and an area where you can take an exam for whatever class you want to be.
A lot of your time in Fortune’s Weave will be spent using these facilities to increase your weapon levels, boost support with your allies, and acquire better equipment.
If I were to nitpick, I’d argue that the support grind can become a little tiresome for some units. If you want to recruit a new ally who requires a high support level, it can take quite some time to fill the gauge and add them to your team, though some are easier to add to your roster than others.
There are more things to do, though, like going to the Theater, taking a bath at the Thermae spa, and accepting subquests from distressed townsfolk. Perhaps the most unusual option, however, is Bird Time.
Here, you can feed the Pale Raven (the main protagonist in bird form) to increase your support level for later in the game. Is it a bit goofy? Yeah. Does it get a bit repetitive? Sure. But I kinda love the feeling of getting that sweet ‘perfect bird time’ message when you have a successful interaction with your ally.
Outside of Dagsion, you can enter the aforementioned dungeons, search for materials, enter into some smaller hub areas, and speak with wandering merchants. The world map is easy to navigate, but you’ll only have a set amount of time to explore before the day of the Main Quest arrives. This helps the game to maintain good pacing throughout, and while there’s a ton to explore, it’s broken up with main story goodness in healthy intervals, in my view.
On a technical level, Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is pretty solid too. It keeps a lot of the enticing visual style seen in Fire Emblem: Three Houses, but being a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, there’s a clear step-up in terms of resolution, and character models look excellent too. Be it Fortuna, whose vibrant hair pops with eye-catching yellow, or the striking, rich reds of Bertrand, the White-Maned Demon’s clothing, I found myself impressed by the visuals pretty consistently.
Some background textures do look a bit basic, however, and while the game runs smoothly, it’s not targeting a silky 60fps (but this never bothered me, personally).
I also want to shout out the game’s excellent soundtrack, which is more eclectic than you may think. There’s the classic orchestral-style stuff, which creates a real sense of grandeur and high stakes, but there are also spacey, synth-led tunes in the temples, which create ambience and intrigue, as well as electronic music with pumping bass in some mysterious hidden areas.
On the topic of sound, the voice acting is exceptional in Fortune’s Weave. You feel each character’s unmistakable personality through just about every performance, and this only makes you feel more attached to your units. The perfect example is Fabio, whose voice acting is just as outlandish and unusual as you’d hope for the character, though he also has some authentic, impassioned emotional scenes that stole the show. Great stuff all round.
To conclude, then, Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is a masterful tactical JRPG that has it all. Addictive, depth-filled combat, fresh mechanics, a well-paced, multi-layered story, and a likeable cast of characters. It hypnotized me from minute one, all the way to the end, and its careful balance of tight turn-based gameplay and exploration really worked for me. As things stand, I consider Fortune’s Weave to not only be among the best Fire Emblem games in recent memory, but also the best game on the Nintendo Switch 2 thus far.
Whatever you do, don’t skip this one.
Should you play Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave?
Play it if…
You want to sink your teeth into an epic RPG
Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is a huge game that will easily take you north of 100 hours to finish if you want to complete each Flame Lord’s path and clear every subquest. If you’re looking for a true epic to get your money’s worth out of, this is the game for you.
You’re a fan of character-driven narratives
Yes, Fortune’s Weave features a very high-stakes story, but the narrative is largely centered around the four Flame Lords, and their personal ambitions in the Heroic Games. Watching each story unfurl, and seeing how each hero develops is a joy, so if you’re into more character-driven stories, then you’ll likely enjoy this.
Don’t play it if…
You’re not a big fan of tactical combat
There are some light action segments and swifter turn-based dungeon battles in Fortune’s Weave, but a lot of the time will be spent commanding your units on a grid. If you’re not into the more strategic style of other Fire Emblem games, then you may not have the best time with this one either.
You need top-tier performance from your games
While Fortune’s Weave looks pretty solid, it’s by no means pushing boundaries as far as visuals go. It’s very stable, in terms of performance, but it’s also not going to give you the buttery smoothness of other Switch 2 games, like Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, say, which can even run at 120fps in handheld mode.
Accessibility features
There are a handful of ways to customize your experience in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave. You can make UI adjustments, like altering the size of the battle minimap, toggling the grid display on and off, you can personalize camera controls and sensitivity, and choose from a number of different subtitle languages.
There’s even an Enemy Masking mode that changes the appearances of insectile enemies if you have arachnophobia or entomophobia. There is no colorblind mode, or similar.
How I reviewed Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave
I spent just over 200 hours with Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, during which time I played through the main story (including each of the Flame Lords’ individual paths), completed just about every subquest, and recruited countless allies.
For the most part, I played in docked mode, with my Nintendo Switch 2 connected to my Sky Glass Gen 2 TV and Marshall Heston 120 soundbar. However, I did dip into handheld mode now and then, and usually had my Sennheiser CX 80U wired earbuds connected when playing on the go.
More generally, I’ve spent years reviewing gaming software, hardware, and accessories here at TechRadar, where I serve as a Senior Reviews Writer. I’ve covered all sorts of titles, from Switch 2 exclusives like Kirby Air Riders and Yoshi and the Mysterious Book to RPGs such as Dragon Quest I & II HD-2D Remake and Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles.
I've also played a number of Fire Emblem titles, including Awakening, The Blazing Blade, and Three Houses.
Harry is a Senior Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He reviews everything from party speakers to wall chargers and has a particular interest in the worlds of audio and gaming. Harry has a background in business tech journalism, particularly around the telecoms industry.

articles.title: Jensen Huang thinks China will develop its own advanced lithography chipmaking tools by 2030 — Nvidia CEO says achievement of that capability 'is just a matter of time'
articles.text:
Jensen Huang thinks China will develop its own advanced lithography chipmaking tools by 2030 — Nvidia CEO says achievement of that capability 'is just a matter of time'
But it remains to be seen just how advanced those systems will be
China's progress toward technological self-sufficiency in recent years is undeniable, but there is one thing that the country has so far failed to develop: lithography tools that are on par with those offered by ASML. That shortcoming has greatly hampered its domestic semiconductor industry. But Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes China will develop its own advanced lithography systems in just three or four years.
"They are going to get there by 2030," Huang said in an interview with The All-In Podcast (at 43:43). "2030 is just around the corner. The way to think about China is that it is really good at high-volume production. It is just a matter of time[...] so two or three years is just a click; it is nothing. So as far as they are concerned, they are already there."
Huang tends to look optimistically at China's technological development. Specifically, he is known for calling China's AI industry as being 'right behind' American frontier labs, which may well be correct, given how much capital China is investing in AI. But when it comes to the Chinese semiconductor industry in general and its lithography sector in particular, Huang may be too optimistic.
At present, China's leading producer of lithography tools — Shanghai Micro Electronics Equipment — can mass-produce a 193-nm ArF dry scanner that can be used to build chips on 90nm-class process technology. While the company has reportedly developed a 28nm-capable ArF immersion scanner, there is no public evidence that such systems are produced in volume and are used for high-volume chip production.
Although there are reports that Shanghai Aishengna Electronic Technology Group (a unit, or an affiliate of SMEE) has delivered its first immersion scanner that may be capable of printing chips using 28nm-class process technology, these tools will require extensive qualification before they can be used for high-volume manufacturing of semiconductors, so if deployment follows standard timelines, it will take years before this unit will be used for mass producing chips.
Even assuming that the first scanners are delivered to Chinese chipmakers in 2026, widespread production use before 2028–2029 appears unlikely. Furthermore, matching the capabilities of an early-generation ASML immersion scanner would still leave Chinese lithography suppliers considerably behind ASML's contemporary systems, which makes technological parity in ArF immersion lithography by 2030 highly unlikely.
China is considerably further behind in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography. While there are reports that Chinese scientists have managed to develop a laser-produced plasma source that can generate the 13.5-nanometer wavelength light required for the technology, it does not look like China is close to assembling even a prototype EUV scanner itself.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Even if China can assemble an EUV experimental exposure platform without having mastered production-quality immersion DUV, it is hard to imagine a Chinese company producing EUV scanners without solving the hardest problems common to both DUV and EUV technologies. A production lithography scanner requires extraordinary capabilities in wafer and reticle stages, alignment, overlay, projection optics, and metrology, just to name a few.
If China is still struggling to industrialize these capabilities for immersion DUV, there is little reason to assume it has somehow solved them at the substantially more demanding EUV level. But given the potentially existential stakes of the AI race, and the determination of the Chinese government to achieve technological self-sufficiency, it may just indeed be a matter of time.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Diesen Flugsimulator kannst du ganz entspannt zocken – sogar mit geschlossenen Augen
articles.text:
Keine Lust auf Stress im Cockpit? Bei diesem Flugsimulator kannst du dich zurücklehnen
Flugsimulatoren wie der Microsoft Flight Simulator haben ihren ganz eigenen Reiz. Obwohl das Steuern eines virtuellen Flugzeuges ein erhabenes Gefühl hervorbringen kann, geht es auch oftmals mit Stress einher. Gerade, wenn die Simulatoren auf einen besonders hohen Realitätsgrad setzen. Doch was wäre, wenn du den Flugsimulator einfach ganz entspannt zocken könntest? Und das sogar mit geschlossenen Augen?
Ein Flugsimulator in der Economy-Class
Das Spiel „Inflight Simulator“ setzt dich nämlich nicht ins Cockpit, sondern auf einen Passagiersitz. Statt dir Gedanken über die Steuerung des gesamten Flugzeuges zu machen, kannst du dich einfach zurücklehnen und anderen das Fliegen überlassen. Zunächst musst du dafür eine Strecke aussuchen. Denn der „Inflight Simulator“ simuliert komplette Flüge. Es gibt lediglich eine Reichweitenbegrenzung. Du kannst also nicht von einer Seite der Erde zur entgegengesetzten Seite fliegen.
Trotzdem sind lange Flüge möglich, die etwa zehn Stunden andauern. Hast du deine Wahl getroffen, geht der Flug auch schon los. Zum Start kannst du dich anschnallen, den Tisch hochklappen und schon einen ersten Blick aus dem Fenster werfen. Ist das Flugzeug erst einmal in der Luft, gibt es aber noch mehr Möglichkeiten.
Denn dann kannst du deinen Sitz auch verlassen und das Flugzeug zu Fuß erkunden. Im „Inflight Simulator“ bist du der oder die einzige Passagier:in. Deshalb kannst du dir Platz (außer im Cockpit) aussuchen und musst nicht warten, dass die Bordtoilette frei wird. Tatsächlich kannst du auch über einen globalen Chat mit anderen Spieler:innen chatten, die ebenfalls Flüge „absolvieren“. So vergeht die Zeit auch etwas schneller.
Apropos Zeit: Besonders praktisch ist, dass du nicht permanent den Browser geöffnet haben musst, um deinen Flug zu genießen. Du kannst auch später wiederkommen. In der Zwischenzeit wird der Flug weiter simuliert. Und wer es etwas abenteuerlicher und unbequemer haben will, kann vom großen Linienflugzeug auch zu einer kleinen Cessna wechseln. Wir empfehlen allerdings, die Lautstärke des Spiels dann etwas herunterzudrehen oder den Sound des Cessna-Motors in den Optionen auszuschalten.

articles.title: Amazon gives its workers a raise of $1 per hour | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon is raising the minimum starting pay for its U.S. core operations workers — like delivery drivers and fulfillment center employees — to $20 per hour and its average hourly pay to nearly $24 per hour. The company notes the higher pay represents an increase of $1 per hour for eligible employees.
“When you add in the value of our industry-leading benefits, average total compensation comes to more than $32 per hour,” Amazon Senior Vice President Udit Madan wrote in a blog post.
The investment in these raises comes out to over $1.5 billion, or about 0.06% of its $2.68 trillion market cap.
In addition, Amazon says it will now also provide employees with access to a low-cost banking system called Day 1 Financial, a membership in First Tech Federal Credit Union, as well as a 20% discount on purchases bought in-store at Whole Foods Market, the premium grocery chain that Amazon owns. If employees order groceries online via Amazon, they will also get a 10% discount.
Amazon already offers its employees free Prime memberships, prepaid education programs, and healthcare coverage, among its benefits.
On a subreddit for Amazon fulfillment center employees, people seem less than enthused. Regarding the Whole Foods discount, one worker commented, “So it would make it cost almost the same as a regular store, then? Hahaha,” a reference to Whole Foods’ historically higher prices.

articles.title: RAMXEED ULTIMATE FeRAM: 10 Years Data Retention - EE Times
articles.text:
RAMXEED is launching a new ferroelectric memory (FeRAM) product line under the brand name RAMXEED ULTIMATE. The lineup features memory products that guarantee 10 years of continuous data retention even under constant exposure to temperatures of 125°C. This level of reliability significantly reduces memory-related constraints and lightens the development burden for system designers working on demanding applications, including automotive systems and industrial factory equipment that require long-term data retention in high-temperature environments.
● FeRAM with guaranteed 10-year data retention at 125°C
RAMXEED announced a groundbreaking nonvolatile memory solution that guarantees 10-year data retention even under continuous exposure to 125°C in harsh temperature environments. The technology is being introduced under the company’s new ferroelectric memory (FeRAM) brand, RAMXEED ULTIMATE. For applications such as automobiles, factory equipment, and infrastructure devices that require long-term data retention in high-temperature environments, this advancement makes it easier to design systems based on the assumption of long-term data retention even under high-temperature conditions.
With the rapid advances in AI integration and digital transformation (DX), data has become more valuable than ever. In recent years, a wide range of systems involving automotive technologies and industrial factory equipment have become deeply integrated with advanced sensors, accelerating the use of sensor-generated data for predictive maintenance, real-time monitoring, and system automation.
As a result, the need for high-frequency data logging is quickly growing, driving the surge in demand for FeRAM. “Historically, sensor memory was primarily used in the relatively mild environments of utility meters and measuring instruments where standard flash memory was sufficient,” explains Yukinobu Hikosaka, General Manager of the FeRAM Technology Department within RAMXEED’s Device Technology Division. “However, modern factory equipment and automotive systems require far more detailed, high-frequency data recording. This shift is steadily broadening the applications for FeRAM and allowing industries to fully leverage its unique strengths, namely, the high endurance of 100 trillion write cycles and ultra-fast data rewrites on the order of tens of nanoseconds,” adds Hikosaka.
With the gradual adoption of FeRAM in factories, automobiles, and other applications, a key consideration is whether the memory unit can reliably retain data for extended periods in high-temperature environments. “In particular, how many years a device can retain data at 125°C, which is considered the benchmark for high-temperature reliability required in automotive and industrial applications, has become the definitive indicator of the true capabilities of memory,” says Hikosaka.
The defining feature of the RAMXEED ULTIMATE FeRAM brand is the official guarantee of a 10-year data retention lifespan at 125°C across both the AEC-Q100-compliant automotive-grade and industrial-grade product lines.
● Even with a standard 125°C rating, actual data retention may be limited to just one year
While the most fundamental characteristic of nonvolatile storage solutions like FeRAM is “data retention,” maintaining data for extended periods in high-temperature environments remains a major technical hurdle for the industry. For FeRAM, higher temperatures accelerate the degradation of the ferroelectric polarization state, which shortens the data retention lifespan.
Paying close attention to the information in the datasheet specifications is therefore crucial. Even if a product claims to support 10 or more years of data retention at 125°C, this performance is often based on the assumption that exposure to 125°C will occur for only about 10% of the product’s overall operating lifespan. “Consequently, if the device is continuously subjected to a constant temperature of 125°C in real-world applications, the actual data retention time drops dramatically and may be as short as one year,” warns Hikosaka.
Hikosaka points out that even when the specification is “10 or more years of data retention at 125°C”, understanding what “125°C” actually means is critical. “Evaluation conditions and baseline assumptions vary significantly for memory products,” he notes. “For memory manufacturers and the customers using these devices, a full understanding of the specific prerequisites behind any 125°C/10-year claim and the significance of that rating is extremely important.”
In contrast, the RAMXEED ULTIMATE series stands apart from typical 125°C rated products by officially guaranteeing a 10-year data retention lifespan under continuous exposure to 125°C.
● Two technologies make long-term data retention under extreme heat possible
Two core technologies make the breakthrough data retention performance of the RAMXEED ULTIMATE series possible: a proprietary manufacturing process technology for ferroelectric capacitors, and the development of highly accurate SPICE models.
Through more than 25 years of FeRAM mass production, RAMXEED has continuously improved the performance of its ferroelectric capacitors. “The ferroelectric capacitor serves as the heart of FeRAM, where the data is actually stored,” says Hikosaka. “Over the years, the company has consistently optimized and improved the material quality, layer configuration, and electrode interfaces for this critical core component,” he adds.
RAMXEED has succeeded in significantly improving data retention characteristics at high temperatures for this new product line by upgrading the quality of the lead zirconate titanate (PZT) ferroelectric thin film and refining the interface structure between the ferroelectric film and the electrodes.
When FeRAM operates continuously at high temperatures, the ferroelectric capacitors degrade over time, leading to a phenomenon known as “imprinting,” which makes data rewriting difficult. For example, if a data value of “1” is retained for an extended period, shifting it to “0” requires a substantially higher voltage, making it difficult to rewrite. By optimizing the manufacturing process, RAMXEED has dramatically enhanced its resistance to imprinting and similar issues. As a result, the company now guarantees that data can be safely retained, read, and successfully rewritten through the entire operating temperature range of -40°C to 125°C.
However, manufacturing process improvements alone did not secure sufficient operating margin for the finished product. Enhancements to circuit design became vital for operating the FeRAM.
RAMXEED developed a proprietary ferroelectric SPICE model that highly accurately replicates the actual measured electrical characteristics of ferroelectric capacitors. This SPICE model reproduces the polarization of a ferroelectric capacitor at any given voltage, matching measured values with exceptional precision. The model was constructed by accounting for manufacturing variations in the FeRAM, as well as other potential data fluctuations.
“By designing circuits with a SPICE model that accounts for variations, devices can reliably distinguish between 1s and 0s even after 10 years of use at 125°C, effectively minimizing the risk of failure,” explains Hikosaka.
● Freeing system designers from memory-related constraints
By adopting RAMXEED ULTIMATE, customers can significantly simplify system design. In the past, ensuring reliable, long-term data retention imposed a variety of constraints on engineering effort and costs, such as limiting the equipment’s operating temperature, reducing runtime hours, or adding backup systems. With RAMXEED ULTIMATE, systems can now be designed with the baseline assumption of 10 years of data retention under continuous exposure to 125°C, thereby eliminating many of these memory-related constraints. This dramatically reduces the overall burden on system and equipment designers.
For example, a major advantage is the equipment’s thermal design. FeRAM is frequently installed near high-performance semiconductor ICs, such as SoCs (Systems on Chip) or microcontrollers. These ICs generate intense heat during processing, and the nearby FeRAM is immediately exposed to high temperatures. Since the RAMXEED ULTIMATE series can retain data without issue even when exposed to the heat generated by these operating ICs, the complexity of the thermal design is significantly reduced compared to conventional solutions.
“Ensuring long-term data retention at high temperatures means much more than simply having a highly reliable memory device,” Hikosaka emphasizes. “It injects flexibility into the overall system design and makes it easier to build systems that offer total peace of mind over years of continuous operation. I am convinced that RAMXEED ULTIMATE brings immense value to designers and, ultimately, to end users,” concludes Hikosaka.
● Over a quarter-century of FeRAM expertise
RAMXEED originated from Fujitsu Semiconductor Memory Solution, a spinoff of Fujitsu’s semiconductor division. The company initiated FeRAM development while still part of Fujitsu and commenced mass production in 1999. Over the past quarter century, the company has supplied FeRAM worldwide and ships to more than 60 countries and regions, with its products used in more than 200 different applications. Cumulative shipments now total 4.4 billion units. “While FeRAM is a niche category within nonvolatile memory, we built a highly successful business around it. FeRAM has already become an integral part of society’s infrastructure,” says Hikosaka. “We take pride in the fact that RAMXEED is not a startup but an established semiconductor manufacturer with a proven track record of mass-producing FeRAM and continuously refining its technology.”
● Achieving 125°C rated performance in the truest sense of the term
The RAMXEED ULTIMATE series represents the pinnacle of the advanced design and manufacturing technologies that RAMXEED has refined over more than 25 years. “By organically combining and integrating all of the previously mentioned elements of material technology for ferroelectric capacitors, process technology to stabilize them at high temperatures, construction of SPICE models, and circuit design that accurately represents their characteristics while accounting for variations and the evaluation technology that translates into product warranties, the company made it possible to guarantee a 10-year data retention lifespan at 125°C,” emphasizes Hikosaka.
By guaranteeing error-free data retention under continuous exposure to 125°C for a full 10 years, the RAMXEED ULTIMATE series achieves 125°C-rated performance in the truest sense of the term. This breakthrough frees system designers from traditional hardware constraints and contributes significantly to accelerating hardware design.

- RAMXEED Limited: RAMXEED ULTIMATE
- Tech Column: Inside RAMXEED ULTIMATE: The Technologies Behind Guaranteed 125°C, 10-Year Data Retention

articles.title: 7 Roald Dahl quotes that reveal life's biggest lessons
articles.text:
7 Roald Dahl quotes that reveal life's biggest lessons
Discover 7 Roald Dahl quotes that reveal powerful lessons about kindness, courage, imagination, and living a meaningful life.
Roald Dahl is best known for creating magical worlds filled with giant peaches, chocolate factories, friendly giants, and extraordinary children.
While his stories are often shelved as children's literature, many of his most memorable lines contain wisdom that resonates just as deeply with adults.
Beneath the humour, adventure, and imagination lies a collection of life lessons about kindness, courage, resilience, and the importance of staying true to yourself.
Part of what makes Dahl's work timeless is his ability to express profound truths in simple, memorable ways. His characters face bullies, overcome obstacles, and discover the power of curiosity and kindness. These themes continue to inspire readers decades after his books were first published.
7 Roald Dahl quotes that reveal some of life's biggest lessons
1. “A person who has good thoughts cannot ever be ugly.”
This memorable quote from The Twits reminds readers that true beauty comes from within. Roald Dahl believed that kindness, generosity, and a positive outlook shape how others see us far more than physical appearance ever could.
In a world obsessed with looks and perfection, the quote offers a refreshing lesson. Character, compassion, and the way we treat people leave a lasting impression. While appearances may change over time, a good heart and kind spirit have the power to make someone truly beautiful.
2. “Never grow up... always down.”
This playful quote reflects Roald Dahl's belief that adults should never completely lose the curiosity, imagination, and sense of wonder they had as children. Throughout his books, the most memorable characters are often those who remain open-minded, adventurous, and willing to see magic in ordinary things.
The quote serves as a reminder that growing older does not have to mean becoming cynical or unimaginative. Keeping a childlike sense of curiosity can help people stay creative, adaptable, and excited about life. Some of life's greatest discoveries happen when we continue to ask questions, explore new ideas, and embrace the world with fresh eyes.
3. “A little magic can take you a long way.”
While Dahl's stories are filled with fantastical elements, this quote speaks to something very real: the power of imagination.
Life can become routine and predictable, but imagination allows people to dream, innovate, and see possibilities where others see limitations. Whether through creativity, optimism, or curiosity, a little "magic" often helps people navigate challenges and discover new opportunities.
4. “Never do anything by halves if you want to get away with it. Be outrageous. Go the whole hog.”
This humorous quote reflects Dahl's appreciation for boldness and enthusiasm. While it is delivered with characteristic wit, it contains an important lesson about commitment.
Success often requires full effort and genuine dedication. Whether pursuing a goal, developing a skill, or chasing a dream, half-hearted attempts rarely produce extraordinary results. Dahl encourages readers to embrace life with energy and conviction.
5. “The more risks you allow your children to make, the better they learn to look after themselves.”
Although written about children, this quote contains wisdom for people of all ages. Growth often requires stepping outside comfort zones and learning through experience.
Mistakes and setbacks are not signs of failure; they are opportunities to learn. By embracing challenges rather than avoiding them, individuals develop confidence, resilience, and independence.
6. “Life is more fun if you play games.”
This simple yet powerful quote reflects one of Roald Dahl's favourite themes: the importance of imagination, playfulness, and not taking life too seriously. Throughout his stories, characters often find joy and adventure by embracing creativity and seeing the world differently.
As adults, it's easy to become consumed by responsibilities and routines. Dahl's words serve as a reminder that happiness often comes from maintaining a sense of fun, curiosity, and spontaneity. Life may be filled with challenges, but approaching it with a playful spirit can make the journey far more enjoyable.
7. “A little nonsense now and then, is relished by the wisest men.”
This witty quote reminds readers that life is not meant to be taken all the time seriously. Roald Dahl understood that humour, playfulness, and moments of silliness are just as important as hard work and responsibility.
In a world that often celebrates productivity and achievement, the quote encourages people to make room for joy. Whether it's laughing with friends, pursuing a hobby, or simply embracing life's absurd moments, a little nonsense can bring balance and happiness. Sometimes, wisdom is not about being serious all the time; it's about knowing when to enjoy life and have fun.
Why Roald Dahl's quotes still matter
Roald Dahl's stories continue to captivate readers because they explore universal truths through imagination. His books celebrate courage over fear, kindness over cruelty, and curiosity over conformity.
Though written for children, Dahl's quotes offer insights that remain relevant to adults. They encourage readers to stay curious, embrace imagination, face challenges with courage, and believe in their ability to make a difference.
Perhaps that is why his stories endure. Long after the final page, their lessons continue to inspire wonder, kindness, and optimism.

articles.title: EDF s’associe au constructeur chinois BYD et provoque un torrent de critiques
articles.text:
En France, les certificats d’économies d’énergie (CEE) imposent aux fournisseurs d’énergie de financer les initiatives permettant d’économiser de l’énergie, en fonction de leur niveau d’activité. L’achat d’un nouveau véhicule électrique par un particulier ou un professionnel peut donc donner droit à une prime CEE. La prime peut s’élever à quelques centaines, voire plusieurs milliers d’euros, selon le profil de l’acheteur et l’éco-score du véhicule. Point important : la marque du véhicule acheté, et donc sa nationalité, n’a pas d’incidence sur l’octroi de cette prime. Justement, EDF vient de nouer un nouveau partenariat avec le géant automobile chinois BYD, mais cela passe mal auprès de certaines personnalités politiques.
Primes CEE : EDF s’associe au constructeur chinois BYD
EDF a annoncé un partenariat avec le constructeur BYD. Le fournisseur d’énergie permet ainsi aux clients français de bénéficier de la prime CEE d’EDF lors de l’achat ou de la location longue durée de certains véhicules électriques de la marque chinoise. Dans le cadre de cette opération commerciale, les particuliers peuvent obtenir 365 euros de remise s’ils choisissent l’achat ou la location longue durée de certains modèles électriques de BYD. Sont concernés la Dolphin Surf, l’Atto 2, l’Atto 3 Evo ainsi que le Sealion 7. Le montant de l’aide est porté à 555 euros pour les clients professionnels.
Autant dire que ce partenariat entre EDF et BYD a suscité de vives réactions chez plusieurs personnalités politiques françaises, aussi bien à gauche qu’à droite. Le problème soulevé est bien entendu la nationalité chinoise du constructeur BYD et donc un coup porté au protectionnisme européen. EDF travaille avec le groupe allemand Volkswagen dans le cadre des primes CEE, notamment pour les marques Volkswagen, Audi, SEAT et Škoda, sans que cela ne suscite de vives réactions.
Un partenariat franco-chinois qui passe mal
Sur X, le député Place Publique Sacha Houlié a déploré ce partenariat : « À quel moment une société 100 % détenue par l’État français favorise-t-il un industriel étranger (et pas n’importe lequel !) contre ses propres constructeurs ! À quoi servent les ministres en charge ?! Quel scandale ! ». Quelques jours plus tard, il a précisé : « les investissements des européens doivent servir notre base industrielle et nos emplois ». De son côté, Marie-Claire Carrère-Gée, sénatrice LR, a déclaré : « Scandaleux et irresponsable : EDF, société nationale, subventionne les voitures électriques chinoises de BYD, via les certificats d’économie d’énergie payés in fine par le consommateur d’électricité français ! ».
Ce partenariat fait même réagir au plus haut sommet de l’État. Selon le journal économique Les Echos, le gouvernement somme EDF de cesser son partenariat avec le chinois BYD d’ici la fin de l’année. Toujours selon Les Echos, le ministre de l’Industrie, Sébastien Martin, a rappelé à EDF que « l’argent public des Européens doit d’abord soutenir notre base industrielle et nos emplois ». Reste maintenant à savoir si les pressions exercées sur l’électricien, détenu à 100 % par l’État, conduiront bel et bien à la fin de ce partenariat entre EDF et le chinois BYD.

articles.title: BYD ya tenía el barco más grande del mundo para transportar sus coches. Ahora va a por diez más
articles.text:
BYD está conquistando el panorama internacional con sus turismos dentro de un ecosistema cada vez más electrificado. Sin embargo, para seguir a ese vertiginoso ritmo hacen falta más barcos y más grandes que puedan transportar sus coches. Y en este sentido, la compañía está redoblando su apuesta por su propia flota de transporte marítimo.
Según cuentan desde New Ships, el fabricante de automóviles chino ha realizado un pedido de diez buques para transportar sus automóviles y camiones, cada uno capaz de transportar unos 9.200 vehículos. Así que todo apunta a que la división de logística marítima de la empresa está a punto de crecer considerablemente. Te contamos todos los detalles.
Sus propios barcos. Además de sus coches, BYD también construye los barcos que los transportan. Y esto es una gran ventaja para la compañía, ya que poseer una flota dedicada se carga de golpe uno de los mayores cuellos de botella a los que se enfrentan los fabricantes de automóviles chinos en este momento, que es precisamente la escasez mundial de capacidad de buques para transportar vehículos.
A medida que las exportaciones se disparan, tener el control total de la cadena logística otorga a BYD una gran ventaja que buena parte de sus competidores no posee, pues normalmente suelen alquilar sus propios espacios de carga.
En detalle. Según se informa, los nuevos buques serán construidos por China Merchants Industry en sus astilleros de Jinling y Haimen, con entregas escalonadas entre 2027 y 2029, según afirman desde New Ships. Una vez entregados, ampliarían la flota propia de BYD de ocho a 18 barcos, superando la capacidad total los 130.000 CEU (unidades equivalentes a automóviles).
La flota actual de la empresa se completó en menos de dos años, habiéndose entregado el primer barco, Explorer No. 1, en enero de 2024, según apuntan desde CarNewsChina.
Visto de cerca. Para poner la escala en perspectiva, el BYD Shenzhen, que zarpó en 2025, ya era el portavehículos más grande del mundo, con capacidad para 9.200 vehículos. La flota original de ocho barcos dio a BYD la capacidad de exportar alrededor de 1 millón de coches al año. Añadir diez buques más de tamaño similar elevaría aproximadamente esa cifra a 2,5 millones de coches al año, según las estimaciones de CarNewsChina.
Cifras. BYD exportó 184.000 vehículos de pasajeros desde China solo en agosto, un 131 % más interanual, según datos de la Asociación de Automóviles de Pasajeros de China. Eso representa más de un tercio de las exportaciones de vehículos de nuevas energías del país. De enero a agosto, BYD envió más de 1,1 millones de vehículos al extranjero, un 88 % más que en el mismo período del año anterior.
Sin embargo, en su propio mercado la cosa cambia drásticamente. Y es que la marca principal de BYD vendió 184.000 coches en China en agosto, un 35 % menos interanual, y las ventas nacionales en lo que va de año han bajado un 43 %, según CarNewsChina. La empresa se encuentra atrapada en medio de una brutal guerra de precios entre más de 100 marcas de vehículos eléctricos, y los márgenes de beneficio de todo el sector automotriz en China habrían caído a tan solo el 3,2 % en el primer trimestre de 2026.

articles.title: La version française de WhatsApp s'emmêle les pinceaux avec son option de confidentialité avancée
articles.text:
Mi-septembre, un lecteur de Numerama nous a écrit pour nous signaler qu’une fonctionnalité de WhatsApp souffrait d’un contre-sens manifeste.
Le couac concerne la « Confidentialité avancée de la discussion », une option censée empêcher les autres membres d’un groupe ou d’une conversation d’exporter l’historique des échanges, d’enregistrer automatiquement les médias reçus dans leur galerie, ou encore de solliciter Meta AI pour résumer ou analyser les messages.
Sauf que, selon la capture d’écran envoyée par notre lecteur, le message affiché dans l’application dit tout l’inverse. On peut y lire que si le réglage est activé, les membres de la discussion « pourront » enregistrer les médias, interroger Meta AI et exporter la conversation, soit précisément ce que la fonctionnalité est censée bloquer.
Un bug franco-français
Par mesure de vérification, nous avons consulté la documentation officielle pour confirmer le fonctionnement prévu à l’origine.
Évidemment, une fois activée, la Confidentialité avancée, mise en place en avril 2025, bloque l’export de la discussion, désactive le téléchargement automatique des médias vers la galerie, et coupe l’accès aux fonctions Meta AI dans le fil concerné. C’est bien une négation qui devrait figurer dans le texte français, quelque chose comme « ne pourront plus ».
Le problème ne semble toucher que la version française de l’application. Nous avons testé les versions anglaise et allemande de WhatsApp, et la négation y est bien présente dans les deux cas !
Difficile de savoir depuis quand cette erreur de traduction s’est glissée dans l’application.
Nous avons signalé le problème à Meta et mettrons cet article à jour dès que nous aurons une réponse de leur part.

articles.title: Le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro passe sous les 300€ grâce à un code promo
articles.text:
Le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro est un téléphone résistant grâce à la certification IP68 et son écran certifié Gorilla Glass Victus 2 efficace contre les chutes. Sur AliExpress, il perd plus de 30 euros sur son prix.
Au début de l’année 2026, le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro a débarqué dans les rayons. Ce smartphone était un mélange entre continuité et innovation et la marque chinoise semble tourner son téléphone vers les sorties longues. Preuve en est, cette autonomie redoutable de deux jours et la luminosité qui dépasse les 3 000 nits. En cette période de French Week d’AliExpress, la version 5G de 256 Go passe sous les 280 euros grâce au code FWFR30.
Le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro est à découvrir pour 271,89 euros au lieu de 306,42 euros
Pourquoi choisir le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro ?
- Pour sa batterie généreuse : Avec 6 600 mAh, le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro embarque la plus grosse batterie de la gamme et il assure une autonomie de deux jours.
- Un écran très lumineux : La dalle de 6,83 pouces offre une luminosité de 3 200 nits, soit le double de celle du Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro.
- Un prix accessible : En passant sous les 280 euros, le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro s’offre l’un des meilleurs rapports qualité-prix sur le secteur de l’entrée de gamme et il arrive à faire oublier ses limites.
Parti pour durer
Pour se démarquer sur le secteur de l’entrée de gamme, Xiaomi mise sur les sorties en extérieur. Pour pouvoir offrir des sorties sans crainte, il faut s’appuyer sur plusieurs critères et le Redmi Note 15 Pro coche toutes les cases. D’abord, il possède la certification IP68, ce qui lui permet de plonger jusqu’à un mètre de profondeur tandis que son écran certifié Gorilla Glass Victus 2 lui permet de résister à des chutes de plusieurs mètres.
Qui dit sortie, dit soleil. Pour que le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro soit lisible même lorsque le soleil bat son plein, la marque chinoise frappe fort puisque l’écran OLED de 6,83 pouces dispose d’une luminosité impressionnante de 3 200 nits, soit le double par rapport au Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro. Ainsi, l'écran sera parfaitement lisible même en plein mois de juillet.
Enfin, si vous êtes amené à faire de longues randonnées, vous pouvez tomber à court de batterie, mais cette situation n’arrivera pas avec le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro. Il dispose d'une batterie de 6 600 mAh et la marque assure une autonomie de deux jours.
Il en manque sous le pied
Si le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro est un smartphone d’entrée de gamme, cela implique forcément que des concessions ont dû être faites quelque part. Pour les trouver, il faut d’abord se tourner vers le processeur du smartphone : le Dimensity 7400-Ultra. Cette puce n’a d’ultra que le nom puisque malgré les 8 Go de RAM, la navigation entre les différentes applications peut parfois manquer de fluidité. Sur les jeux gourmands, il est difficile d’atteindre les 60 FPS.
Néanmoins, ce processeur légèrement décevant n’est pas dérangeant si l’on connaît ses limites au moment de l’achat. En revanche, ce qui surprend davantage, c’est l’omniprésence des pubs. Si c'est en quelque sorte la marque de fabrique de Xiaomi, le constructeur a passé un cap avec une vingtaine d’applications qui s’incrustent sur l’écran d’accueil. S’il est possible de les désinstaller, la démarche s’avère assez chronophage.
✅ Les points forts
- Un écran très lumineux
- Deux jours d'’autonomie
- La certification IP68
❌ Les limites
- Peu d’évolution sur les performances
- Trop de pubs
Habituellement vendu pour 306,42 euros, le Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro passe à 271,89 euros sur AliExpress
Entre ses points forts et ses points faibles, une question subsiste : faut-il acheter ce Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro ? La réponse est oui.
