articles.title: Pas de facture mobile avant 2027 : La Poste Mobile offre 4 mois gratuits sur ses forfaits 5G — Frandroid
articles.text:
Ne pas payer son forfait téléphonique jusqu’à la fin de l’année 2026, c’est possible grâce à l’offre proposée par La Poste Mobile sur l’ensemble de ses forfaits sans engagement. Avec cette grande opération séduction, l’opérateur permet donc d’économiser jusqu’à 80 € sans aucune contrepartie.
Pour le forfait La Poste Mobile 130 Go à 10,99 € par mois, vous pouvez profiter de près de 40 € de remise immédiate. Mais il faut faire vite : l’opération s’achève le 4 octobre prochain.
Quatre mois gratuits : comment en profiter ?
La méthode est limpide : La Poste Mobile ne facture tout simplement pas les quatre premiers mois d’abonnement. En cas de souscription, la première facture à régler sera donc celle de janvier. L’économie réalisée est d’environ 80 € si l’on opte pour le forfait le plus garni en data.
Une fois sur le site de La Poste Mobile, il suffit de sélectionner l’offre qui convient parmi les suivantes : 100 Mo de 4G ou 50, 130, 250 et 350 Go de 5G. On décide ensuite si l’on souhaite conserver son numéro de téléphone et le tour est joué.
Pour garder le même numéro de téléphone mobile, il suffit de composer le 3179 depuis la ligne concernée. L’appel est gratuit et vous indique le fameux code RIO (Relevé d’Identité Opérateur). Celui-ci vous est envoyé dans la foulée par SMS et doit être renseigné dans le champ indiqué.
Il suffit ensuite de remplir le formulaire d’informations avec vos données personnelles. La démarche de souscription est simple. La Poste Mobile s’occupe de résilier votre précédent forfait. Votre nouvelle carte SIM, facturée 9,90 €, est ensuite envoyée gratuitement chez vous.
Un forfait qui a tout pour plaire
Le forfait 130 Go inclut la 5G sans surcoût. Les communications sont illimitées en France métropolitaine (et dans les Départements et Collectivités d’Outre-Mer), comme les SMS et MMS.
Une partie de cette enveloppe internet est utilisable sans frais au sein de l’ensemble des pays de l’Union européenne. Jusqu’à 25 Go par mois sont donc disponibles à l’étranger. C’est confortable, même si l’on passe régulièrement plusieurs semaines en vadrouille.
Pour le reste, La Poste Mobile a fait ses preuves :
- points de vente sur tout le territoire ;
- service client disponible 6 jours sur 7 ;
- 20 000 conseillers disponibles ;
- prêt d’un smartphone en cas de perte, casse ou vol.
Il est possible de bloquer le hors forfait directement depuis son espace client. Numéros surtaxés, appels à l’international, data à l’étranger : activer le blocage permet d’éviter toute mauvaise surprise sur sa facture.
Le meilleur réseau français ?
Vous hésitez à changer d’opérateur ? Un élément peut certainement faire pencher la balance. La Poste Mobile utilise l’infrastructure de Bouygues Telecom, qui dispose de plus de 30 000 antennes 4G et 18 000 antennes 5G. Au total, 99 % de la population française est couverte par ce réseau.
Cela permet donc aux abonnés La Poste Mobile de profiter du meilleur réseau disponible dans l’Hexagone. Un baromètre réalisé par l’organisme indépendant nPerf le classe en effet à la première place.
Pour connaître la qualité de la couverture réseau dans votre secteur, des outils sont disponibles comme celui de l’ARCEP ou de La Poste Mobile. À la maison, au travail ou à la salle de sport : découvrez en quelques clics si le débit est bon près de chez vous.

articles.title: Java 27 Delivers Post-Quantum Cryptography, Future Language Innovation, Helidon 27, JavaFX 27
articles.text:
Oracle has released version 27 of the Java programming language and virtual machine. As the second non-LTS release since JDK 25, the final feature set includes nine JEPs, five of which are still progressing through the preview and incubator stages. The JEPs in this final feature set are:
- JEP 523: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector in All Environments
- JEP 527: Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3
- JEP 531: Lazy Constants (Third Preview)
- JEP 532: Primitive Types in Patterns, instanceof, and switch (Fifth Preview)
- JEP 533: Structured Concurrency (Seventh Preview)
- JEP 534: Compact Object Headers by Default
- JEP 536: JFR In-Process Data Redaction
- JEP 537: Vector API (Twelfth Incubator)
- JEP 538: PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects (Third Preview)
This release focuses on strengthening security, future language innovation, and projects under the auspices of the Java Verified Portfolio.
Shown in the graph below, as presented in this blog post by Donald Smith, Vice President of Product Management at Oracle, are the number of cumulative JEPs in each Java release since JDK 8.
Since the release of JDK 24, Oracle has been adding security features that serve as a robust foundation for developers to build more secure applications. As described in this Oracle blog post:
Oracle is executing on a strategy to make post-quantum cryptography (PQC) broadly available across the Java ecosystem with a roadmap that brings standardized PQC algorithms and PQC-enabled TLS to current Long-Term Support (LTS) releases, helping reduce adoption friction for developers and enterprises.
These features include: JEP 496, Quantum-Resistant Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism; JEP 497, Quantum-Resistant Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm; JEP 510, Key Derivation Function API; JEP 527, Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3; and JEP 542, PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects (to be finalized in JDK 28).
PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects (Third Preview)
JEP 538, PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects (Third Preview), proposes a third preview after two rounds of preview delivered in JDK 25 and JDK 26. This feature offers "an API for encoding objects that represent cryptographic keys, certificates, and certificate revocation lists into the widely-used Privacy-Enhanced Mail (PEM) transport format, and for decoding from that format back into objects." This JEP will support conversions between PEM text and cryptographic objects in PKCS #8 and X.509 binary formats. Changes include: a reclassification of the PEM record class to a regular class as a convenience for providing constructors that accept Base64-encoded content in byte arrays; and a rename of the DEREncodable interface to BinaryEncodable to more accurately describe the binary data stored in PEM text.
Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3
JEP 527, Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3, proposes to enhance the implementation of RFC 8446, Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3, using the Hybrid Key Exchange in TLS 1.3 specification, currently being drafted by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) in conjunction with JEP 496, Quantum-Resistant Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism, delivered in JDK 24.
Java Verified Portfolio
Introduced at JavaOne 2026, the Java Verified Portfolio (JVP) is an ecosystem of Oracle-supported technologies. With this release, Helidon 27, JavaFX 27, Jipher 20 and a JVP extension for VS Code were introduced to the Java community.
The release of Helidon 27, now aligned with the OpenJDK versioning, is the first release that follows the Oracle Tip & Tail Model of Library Development. Helidon 27 will serve as the Tip while Helidon 4.5.5, still managed under the familiar semantic versioning, will serve as the Tail. This will allow development teams that require a longer-lived production baseline to remain on the Tail. InfoQ will follow up with a more detailed news story.
The release of JavaFX 27 delivers new features such as: a "metal rendering pipeline on macOS for smoother performance on modern Apple hardware;" enhanced text editing controls; and continued improvements for accessibility. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
The release of Oracle Jipher 20, a Java Cryptographic Service Provider (CSP) that supports FIPS 140-3, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules, delivers notable changes such as: expanded support for additional JDK versions (JDK 17, JDK 21, JDK 25 and JDK 27); and support for the aforementioned security features.
Java 27 Launch Stream
A three-hour JDK 27 launch stream event, hosted by Oracle Developer Advocates Ana-Maria Mihalceanu, Billy Korando and Nicolai Parlog, featured topics such as: performance improvements; security enhancements; Structured Concurrency; Compact Object Headers; JDK Flight Recorder updates; Helidon 27; and agentic AI.
JDK 28 and Future Java Innovation
The formal release date for JDK 28 is expected to be March 2027, soon to be proposed by Mark Reinhold, Chief Architect, Java Platform Group at Oracle. So far, six JEPs have been targeted for JDK 28 and include long-awaited features from Project Valhalla:
- JEP 539, Strict Field Initialization in the JVM (Preview), introduces strictly-initialized fields in the Java Virtual Machine that are required to be initialized before they are read. Therefore, default values such as 0 or null are never observed. This feature is available for use by compilers that emit class files.
- JEP 401, Value Classes and Objects (Preview), proposes to enhance the language with value objects, defined as objects that: only contain final fields; do not have identity; and are solely distinguished by the values of their respective fields.
This marks a significant milestone for Project Valhalla with these two features integrated in the JDK mainline. This will ultimately allow the Vector API to be elevated from Incubation to Preview.
JEP 537, Vector API (Twelfth Incubator), under the auspices of Project Panama, proposes a twelfth incubation, with no substantial implementation changes since JDK 25, after eleven rounds of incubation delivered in JDK 16 through JDK 26. This feature introduces an API to "express vector computations that reliably compile at runtime to optimal vector instructions on supported CPU architectures, thus achieving performance superior to equivalent scalar computations."
Developers can anticipate a JDK 28 feature freeze in early-December 2026. More details on additional JEPs released in JDK 27 and JDK 28 along with other Draft JEPs and candidates may be found in this more detailed InfoQ news story.
JDK 27 may now be downloaded from Oracle with binaries from other vendors expected to become available in the coming days.

articles.title: Xiaomi 18 Fold: Price, release date, specs and features
articles.text:
Table of contents
On September 7, 2026, Xiaomi announced the Xiaomi 18 Fold in China, its company’s first foldable with a wide, short shape, a change from the tall, narrow shape used on past Mix Fold models. The announcement came two days before Apple revealed its own foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, and in the same week as Huawei’s Mate XT2.
If you are in Nigeria and want this phone, there is one thing to know first: Xiaomi has not announced a Nigerian or wider African release.
Xiaomi 18 Fold release date and availability
Xiaomi unveiled the 18 Fold on September 7, 2026. Sales in China began on September 10, with the entry model starting at CNY 10,999. The release currently covers China only. Xiaomi has not given an international launch date.
The timing matters, but you should separate an announcement from a phone reaching shops. Huawei also unveiled its Mate XT2 on September 7, with Chinese sales starting on September 12. Apple announced the iPhone Duo on September 9, but its preorders only open on October 16, and it goes on sale on October 23. If you are in Nigeria and want one now, you are looking at a China-market import. This usually means buying from an independent seller or arranging a purchase through a shipping service.
Xiaomi 18 Fold price
Xiaomi sells the 18 Fold in four standard configurations, plus a Ceramic Special Edition. That gives you five options to pick from.
| Configuration | China price | Approx. US dollars | Approx. naira | 
| 12GB RAM + 256GB | CNY 10,999 | $1,640 | ₦2,249,000 | 
| 12GB RAM + 512GB | CNY 11,999 | $1,789 | ₦2,454,000 | 
| 16GB RAM + 512GB | CNY 12,999 | $1,938 | ₦2,658,000 | 
| 16GB RAM + 1TB | CNY 14,999 | $2,236 | ₦3,067,000 | 
| Ceramic Special Edition, 16GB + 1TB | CNY 15,999 | $2,385 | ₦3,272,000 | 
These dollar and naira figures use the rounded mid-market rates Wise showed on September 16, 2026: CNY 1 equals $0.1491 and ₦204.50. Dollar amounts are rounded to the nearest dollar, and naira amounts to the nearest ₦1,000.
These figures only show what Xiaomi’s China price converts to. A real Nigerian quote will likely add shipping, insurance, import charges, the seller’s margin, and a different exchange rate on the day. Xiaomi has not released an official Nigerian retail price yet.
According to launch coverage, the Ceramic Special Edition has a silicon nitride back and a production limit of 1,500 units. Check stock before you order this version.
Detailed specs
1. Design and durability
The phone measures 117.8 x 83.6 x 10.68mm closed and 117.8 x 163.8 x 5.02mm open. It weighs 219g. Xiaomi sells it in four finishes:
- Black
- Warm Gold White
- Xiye Red
- Pink, on the Ceramic Special Edition
In terms of construction, the phone uses:
- A three-link Dragon Bone hinge
- Dual-layer UTG glass on the folding screen
- A 7000-series aluminium frame
- IP58 and IP59 laboratory ratings, though Xiaomi excludes liquid-immersion damage from its warranty
Think about the shape before you buy. A short body can suit a smaller pocket, but 83.6mm closed is still a wide phone in your hand. A screen’s diagonal measurement alone will not tell you how it feels to hold or type on. If you can, try a similarly wide device first.
2. Display
- Cover screen, 5.38 inches AMOLED, 1712 x 1168 pixels
- Inner screen, 7.58 inches AMOLED, 2364 x 1672 pixels
Both screens run a 1 to 120Hz LTPO refresh rate and reach an advertised peak brightness of 4,000 nits.
Xiaomi describes the shape as close to standard A-series paper, which gives you a wide workspace when open. Remember, peak brightness isn’t a level the whole screen holds all the time.
3. Performance and software
Xiaomi’s own XRING O3 chip powers the 18 Fold. It uses a 3nm process with a 10-core CPU, a 16-core GPU and a four-core NPU built for on-device AI tasks.
Memory changes by storage tier. The 256GB and 512GB models use LPDDR5X, while the 1TB models use LPDDR6. All versions use UFS 4.1 storage. This means paying for 16GB of RAM alone doesn’t guarantee you get LPDDR6.
The phone ships with HyperOS 4. The spec sheet reviewed for this article names the interface but doesn’t state the underlying Android version. It also does not confirm the Android upgrade count, the security support end date, or full English-language support for the AI features. Treat those details as unconfirmed for now.
A chip’s specifications alone cannot tell you how the phone handles sustained gaming, heat, or battery life. Those need real testing on retail software. If you are choosing between memory tiers, weigh the extra storage against the price gap and the apps you actually use.
4. Multitasking and foldable features
HyperOS 4 supports two-app, three-app, and six-app screen arrangements, swipe gestures, and floating windows. Xiaomi also built in a desktop-style WPS mode for office work.
A useful example is keeping a reference document open beside an email draft, or comparing a quotation with a spreadsheet. That shows what the split-screen space can do. It does not mean every Nigerian banking, office, or messaging app has been optimised for this phone.
Xiaomi also promotes a smooth switch between the outer and inner displays. Check whether your most-used apps keep their layout and position when you switch screens on the software version being sold.
Xiaomi’s Super Xiao Ai “Inspiration Ball” assistant is due for an update in late September 2026, and this is subject to change. Do not assume it works today.
5. Camera
- 200MP f/1.7 main camera, with optical stabilisation
- 50MP f/2.4 ultrawide camera
- 50MP f/2.8 periscope telephoto, with optical stabilisation, 3.5x optical zoom and 7x sensor-based zoom
- 16MP f/2.2 front camera, supporting 1080p video at 60fps
The rear cameras record video up to 8K at 24fps or 4K at 60fps.
The dedicated telephoto lens looks useful on paper for portraits and distant subjects. Note that the 7x figure is sensor-based magnification, not a separate 7x optical lens. Megapixel counts alone cannot tell you how the phone handles low light, skin tones, or moving subjects.
6. Battery and charging
The 18 Fold has a 6,000mAh silicon-carbon battery with 20% silicon content. It supports 67W wired charging and 50W wireless charging. Xiaomi includes an adapter in the box, though you need extra compatible equipment to reach the top wireless speed.
Confirm the adapter and wireless charging costs before you import this phone. Battery capacity is only one part of how long a charge lasts. Screen brightness, network signal, gaming, and time spent on the larger display all affect it. No independent battery test result is claimed in this article.
7. Connectivity and SIM
- Dual nano-SIM
- Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0
- NFC and UWB
- USB 3.2 Gen 2
- 5G band n78, plus LTE bands 3, 7, 20 and 28
Xiaomi does not list eSIM support for this model.
These specifications give you details to check with your mobile operator. They do not confirm that every Nigerian network feature, including 5G and voice over LTE, works on this exact China-market unit. Ask for a live demonstration on your network before you buy.
How the Xiaomi 18 Fold compares
The Galaxy Z Fold8 and the iPhone Duo are the two closest rivals in this wider foldable category. The table below uses each brand’s published specifications.
| Feature | Xiaomi 18 Fold | Galaxy Z Fold8 | iPhone Duo | 
| Cover / inner display | 5.38 / 7.58 inches | 5.5 / 7.6 inches | 5.4 / 7.6 inches | 
| Weight | 219g | 201g | 254g | 
| Rear cameras | 200MP main, 50MP ultrawide, 50MP telephoto | 50MP main, 50MP ultrawide | 48MP main, 48MP ultrawide | 
| Battery | 6,000mAh | 4,800mAh | Capacity not stated; Apple claims up to 31 hours of inner-screen video playback | 
Samsung’s page separates the standard Fold8 shown here from the Fold8 Ultra, and Apple’s playback claim cannot be compared directly against a battery figure in milliamp-hours.
Samsung has the lowest weight of the three. Xiaomi has a dedicated telephoto camera and the largest stated battery of the two Android models here. Apple brings a different operating system and app ecosystem, though its October 23 release date is still weeks away. These differences give you a shortlist to work from. They do not settle which phone wins on photography or battery life.
What this means for Nigerian buyers
At the checked exchange rate, the entry model already costs about ₦2.25 million before an importer adds their own charges. Get a written total that covers delivery, any import charges and the seller’s return policy. A currency conversion alone cannot tell you what a shop in Lagos or Abuja will actually charge you.
Pay as much attention to software as you do to hardware. The China launch materials reviewed for this article do not confirm full Google service compatibility for use in Nigeria. Ask the seller to show you Google sign-in, Play Store access, notifications and the specific apps you rely on working. Google explains how to check Play Protect certification under the Play Store’s Settings and About menu, and a Play Store icon on the screen is not proof on its own.
For network access, confirm the exact model with your operator and check coverage where you live and work. MTN says its 5G service needs a compatible device, a 4G-enabled SIM, and 5G coverage in your area. A seller saying a phone “supports 5G” isn’t enough proof that it works on your specific network.
Warranty is the other big question before you pay. Xiaomi’s Nigerian terms generally limit after-sales service to the country where you bought the phone, unless another agreement applies. An imported China unit needs a clear repair plan. Find out who handles repairs, where the phone goes, and who pays for shipping. It is unclear whether replacement screens, hinges, and batteries are available locally for this model.
Xiaomi also advises using its own service team to replace the inner screen protector. Confirm you have a local option for that too.
The Xiaomi 18 Fold offers a compact folding design, a dedicated zoom camera, and a large battery. For a Nigerian buyer, its real value depends on the final delivered price and whether the seller can show you working software, reliable network access, and a clear repair route. Get those answers before you pay.

articles.title: La pause de l'IA divise : Meta refuse de ralentir, Mistral dénonce la stratégie d'OpenAI et Anthropic
articles.text:
Le monde de l’IA a été secoué par plusieurs appels au ralentissement ces derniers jours. Pour Dario Amodei, PDG d’Anthropic, il faut impérativement lever le pied avant que des agents autonomes puissent prendre le contrôle d’Internet. Le dirigeant a mis en avant un plan en trois étapes pour ralentir le rythme des progrès en IA sans freiner l’innovation. Sam Altman, PDG d’OpenAI, a donné raison à son rival, assurant qu’il va prendre des mesures fortes pour améliorer l’évaluation de ses IA.
Même Elon Musk a abondé dans le même sens, suivi, quelques jours plus tard, par Bilal Chughtai, ancien ingénieur de recherche chez Google DeepMind. Le chercheur est persuadé « que l’IA a le potentiel de nous tuer tous et que nous sommes peut-être en train de manquer de temps pour éviter une telle issue ». Dans ce contexte, OpenAI, Google et Anthropic se sont mis à collaborer sur un dispositif commun de supervision des risques de l’intelligence artificielle.
À lire aussi : Selon Anthropic, les plombiers et électriciens pourraient être les grands gagnants de l’IA
Mark Zuckerberg refuse de lever le pied sur l’IA
L’appel du pied lancé par Anthropic et OpenAI n’a pas été bien accueilli par tous les géants de l’IA. Mark Zuckerberg, le patron de Meta, a fermement rejeté l’idée d’un ralentissement de la recherche. Il estime qu’il existe déjà des garde-fous naturels qui peuvent éviter que l’IA ne devienne un danger. Selon lui, « les gens ne voudront pas utiliser des agents IA qui ne sont pas alignés sur leurs intérêts et qui ne font pas ce qu’ils demandent ».
De facto, « les laboratoires ont donc une forte incitation naturelle à rendre leurs modèles davantage alignés ». En clair, tous les géants de l’intelligence artificielle ont déjà intérêt à mettre au point des technologies qui respectent les règles et les restrictions fixées par leurs créateurs. Les impératifs du marché constitueraient des garde-fous suffisants. Zuckerberg réfute l’idée d’un ralentissement et de la mise en place d’un système de régulation. L’alignement, c’est-à-dire la capacité de l’IA à s’aligner sur les valeurs et les désirs des humains, serait un rempart bien suffisant à toutes les dérives. Pour Zuckerberg, « tout laboratoire qui ne se concentre pas sur l’alignement prendra du retard ».
Pour le patron de Meta, tout va bien
Le créateur de Facebook estime que les géants d’IA n’ont pas besoin de nouvelles lois pour prendre des précautions. Celles-ci ont bien assez peur d’être traînées en justice, ce qui constitue là encore un garde-fou. Pour illustrer son propos, il rappelle que Meta a préféré retarder de plusieurs mois la sortie de Muse AI, son système capable de créer des agents personnalisés, le temps de mieux verrouiller la sécurité de l’outil.
 Last month I wrote about how we can build a positive and safe future for everyone: https://t.co/1KtONlqBs5
Every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to take its own actions to ensure that happens.
The…
— Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd) September 15, 2026
Selon le milliardaire, tout est donc déjà en place pour éviter que l’intelligence artificielle fasse des dégâts. A contrario d’Altman et d’Amodei, il avait estimé cet été que rien ne doit reporter l’arrivée de nouvelles IA américaines « ne serait-ce que d’un mois ».
À lire aussi : OpenAI se dit prêt à lever le pied sur l’IA, mais refuse d’être le seul
Mistral AI tacle ses rivaux américains
Dans le sillage de Mark Zuckerberg, Mistral AI, la start-up française de l’IA, refuse d’abonder dans le même sens qu’Anthropic et OpenAI. Dans une déclaration transmise à nos confrères du Figaro, l’entreprise reconnait d’abord les dangers inhérents de l’intelligence artificielle. Il affirme que « les modèles d’IA deviennent des acteurs puissants dès lors qu’on leur donne une marge de manœuvre dans l’exécution et un accès à des outils ». Pour déployer l’IA en toute sécurité, il faut exercer « un véritable contrôle » avec une « séparation rigoureuse des accès ».
Surtout, Mistral accuse, sans citer de nom, les géants de l’IA américains de jouer un double jeu en plaidant pour de nouvelles restrictions, taillées pour noyer la concurrence à leur avantage. Pour la start-up, Anthropic et OpenAI se servent de leurs avertissements à répétition pour conserver le contrôle du marché de l’IA.
Quoi qu’il en soit, les appels à la réglementation n’ont pas trouvé écho auprès de Washington. Donald Trump refuse fermement d’envisager l’idée d’un ralentissement de l’IA. Le président redoute que la moindre pause permette à la Chine de prendre de l’avance sur les États-Unis. Pour enfoncer le clou, Trump a même appelé Jensen Huang, PDG de Nvidia, en plein milieu d’une conférence.

articles.title: Solar panel costs have plummeted from $6 per watt in 2000 to just 12 cents today
articles.text:
The big picture: Cheap solar panels are reshaping the way electricity systems operate from Pakistan to Australia. Businesses and households are generating more of their own power, reducing daytime grid purchases while still relying on utilities to maintain networks and supply electricity when solar output falls. The shift is making demand harder to forecast and prompting grid operators to invest in better system visibility, storage, and new pricing models.
At Bestway Cement's plant in Chakwal, Pakistan, solar already supplies more than a quarter of the electricity used to make cement. The company has 26MW installed and expects to add another 6.34MW by the end of the year.
"It's the only way we can compete," Abdul Waheed, the plant's general manager, told the Financial Times. "Our rivals have already gone in this direction."
The economics are driving the shift. Solar panels that sold for $5 to $6 per watt around 2000 now cost about 12 cents per watt, according to Dave Jones, co-founder of Ember. China's manufacturing expansion is behind much of that decline. Wood Mackenzie estimates Chinese solar manufacturing capacity at roughly 1.36 terawatts.
The lower prices have made rooftop and on-site solar practical in countries where power is costly or unreliable. By the end of 2025, installed small-scale solar capacity worldwide had reached nearly 1.2 terawatts, according to the Energy Institute's Statistical Review of World Energy. While solar does not generate at full capacity around the clock, the installed total is about three times the size of the global nuclear fleet.
Credit: The Financial Times
Businesses have been among the fastest adopters because their peak electricity use often occurs during sunny hours. Ember expects Africa to add about 17GW of solar this year, largely through smaller systems at factories and commercial sites.
In the Philippines, rooftop solar capacity may have nearly doubled in the 12 months through April, Ember says. Meralco, the country's electricity distributor, said rooftop systems generated 372 gigawatt hours in the first six months of the year. Ember estimates that residential systems can now pay for themselves there in a little more than three years.
India is scaling rooftop systems through a national subsidy program launched in February 2024. The program has installed panels on more than 5 million homes and is adding about 500,000 homes a month, according to Tata Power chief executive Praveer Sinha. "It's a democratization of the use of electricity," he said.
But the same trend is putting pressure on utilities. Customers who can afford solar systems and batteries often use less grid power. That reduces utility revenue even though those customers still rely on the grid at night, during cloudy weather, and when their batteries run low.
K-Electric, which supplies Karachi, has seen solar spread through the city's affluent Defence Housing Authority neighborhood. Chief executive Syed Muhammad Taha called solar panels a "curse and a blessing." The customers installing them are among the utility's best-paying users, but they are buying less electricity.
The risk is that costs shift to people who cannot install solar. In Karachi's Lyari district, K-Electric says it loses Rs30 to Rs40 ($0.31 to $0.42) for every Rs100 ($1.04) spent providing electricity. Azem Baloch, a mechanic who rents a flat in the neighborhood, said, "I am spending more than half of my income on power."
South Africa is dealing with a similar problem. Shoprite has installed solar panels on buildings and trucks in South Africa and Namibia since 2015. The retailer now has about 43MW of peak capacity and is considering batteries.
For Eskom, the country's state utility, less demand from businesses and wealthier customers means less revenue for power plants and grid maintenance. Eskom estimates rooftop solar and batteries accounted for around 7% of its 11.7 terawatt-hour decline in electricity sales in the year ended March.
Grid operators also have a technical problem. Solar production can change sharply as weather changes, especially in places with high rooftop adoption. In Australia, midday solar output can push grid demand so low that it becomes harder to operate conventional plants needed to keep the system stable.
Credit: The Financial Times
Rooftop systems can also send excess power from local distribution networks into high-voltage transmission lines, increasing voltage and limiting how much electricity households can export. Forecasting output from millions of small systems has become a major task for grid operators.
Pierluigi Mancarella, chair professor of electrical power systems at the University of Melbourne, said the risk becomes clear when clouds move over areas with heavy rooftop solar use. "If you have a massive cloud formation, the rooftop PV production can drop by so much that it looks like you have lost basically almost a nuclear power station."
Utilities are responding with batteries, new tariff models and better forecasting tools. UK Power Networks recently completed a £389,000 ($523,992) study on machine-learning models to estimate how much solar capacity is connected to its network. Solar forecasting company Amperon retrains its models every hour to account for changing conditions.
The shift is unlikely to slow. Solar is becoming a standard way for businesses and households to lower energy costs, but it is also turning the traditional power grid into a more complex system – one that must handle electricity flowing in both directions.

articles.title: Após críticas, Amazon corrige bug de sideloading no Fire TV • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Após críticas, Amazon corrige bug de sideloading no Fire TV
Atualização no Fire OS desativou acidentalmente a instalação de apps de fontes externas.
Alguns dispositivos da linha Fire TV voltarão a autorizar a instalação de aplicativos de fontes externas. A prática, conhecida no meio da tecnologia como sideloading, estava bloqueada para muitos usuários após atualizações do sistema Fire OS liberadas pela Amazon.
Após uma onda de reclamações, a empresa reconheceu o problema e disse que a limitação não foi intencional. Na verdade, um bug no software, que já teve a causa identificada, será resolvido com um novo patch de correção.
O problema atingiu aparelhos rodando as versões mais recentes do Fire OS 7 e Fire OS 8 e afetou especificamente o menu “Instalar apps desconhecidos”. O sistema da Amazon passou a verificar desnecessariamente todos os aplicativos do dispositivo, incluindo os nativos, antes de gerar a permissão de instalação.
A interface nem sempre aguardava a conclusão dessa varredura, mostrando um menu incompleto ou completamente vazio na tela. Hardwares mais antigos e com processadores menos potentes, como o modelo de entrada Fire TV Stick Lite, foram os mais prejudicados.
A Amazon informou que o patch corretivo será lançado e instalado automaticamente nos dispositivos afetados nos próximos dias. Como a mudança afeta apenas o aplicativo de configurações do sistema, o número da versão do Fire OS não deve ser alterado.
Apesar do alívio para os atuais proprietários, a facilidade de instalar aplicativos de fora da loja da Amazon tem prazo de validade. A fabricante já confirmou que seus futuros dispositivos de streaming deixarão o Android de lado em favor do Vega OS, uma plataforma baseada em Linux. A mudança promete entregar mais fluidez e menor consumo de energia, mas impedirá o uso de pacotes de instalação no formato APK.

articles.title: U.S. and U.K.-based Expanse raises €4.5 million for predictive AI infrastructure platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Expanse, an AI infrastructure company, today announced a €4.5 million ($5.3 million) Seed funding round in order to expand its engineering team, accelerate product development and reach wider industry adoption.
The round was led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from PXN Ventures, AIP Seed, and angel investors including former DeepMind researchers.
“Today, every AI workload begins with an educated guess,” says Ismaeel Bashir, co-founder and CEO of Expanse. “Engineers shouldn’t have to predict exactly how much compute their code will need before they press run. The machine should carry the uncertainty, not the person.”
Expanse’s Seed round can be placed amid broader 2026 investment in the infrastructure and software layers intended to make AI compute more available and efficient.
EU-Startups has reported London-based Callosum raising €85.4 million to route workloads across different AI models and chips, Vienna’s Ora Computing securing €3.5 million for model compression and inference efficiency, Helsinki-based Verda raising €100 million for AI cloud infrastructure, and London-based Nscale closing a €1.7 billion Series C for vertically integrated compute infrastructure.
Other adjacent rounds include €16 million for Switzerland’s AI Infrastructure Capital AG, €5 million for Danish AI infrastructure startup Velatir and €1.7 million for Prague cloud platform Zerops.
Together, these 2026 financings amount to approximately €1.91 billion, or around €1.92 billion including Expanse, although the total is heavily weighted towards Nscale’s round.
The UK is particularly represented in this group through Nscale and Callosum, the latter of which, like Expanse, is developing software intended to allocate AI workloads more efficiently across available compute.
Today’s news comes just one day after Crane Venture Partners announced their €419 million active across four new investment vehicles.
“The future of AI won’t be defined only by who builds the biggest clusters, but by who uses them most intelligently,” adds Scott Sage, co-founder and Partner at Crane Venture Partners. “Expanse gives organisations something they don’t have today: certainty. By predicting exactly what every workload needs before it runs, customers recover existing capacity, reduce waste and extend the life of some of the world’s most valuable infrastructure. We believe that’s a new and important category in AI infrastructure.”
Founded in 2025, Expanse’s software predicts what an AI workload needs before it runs, helping organisations reduce over-allocation, prevent failed jobs and unlock more value from the GPU infrastructure they already own.
Expanse was founded by four University of Edinburgh graduate engineers who previously built and operated large-scale compute infrastructure across quantitative finance and national supercomputing facilities.
While at the Edinburgh Parallel Computing Centre (EPCC), co-founder Ismaeel Bashir developed a multimodal HPC resource prediction system that predicted resource requirements across HPC workloads. Together, Bashir and co-founders Nikodem Bieniek, Eren Mendi, Yafet Melake recognised that even the world’s most sophisticated compute environments still relied on manual estimation to allocate resources efficiently.
Unlike traditional monitoring and observability platforms, which explain what happened after a workload has finished, Expanse says they work before execution begins. Installed directly into an organisation’s cloud or on-premises infrastructure, its models analyse workloads without code or telemetry ever leaving the customer’s environment, allowing organisations to optimise performance while maintaining data sovereignty.
Andy Barrow, Managing Director of PXN Ventures, says: “The widespread adoption of AI by businesses and everyday users has led to an unprecedented focus on the infrastructure required to service this technology and many of the challenges that engineers face. As Expanse has identified, one of those challenges is optimisation and helping businesses to make better use of their compute resource, which can lower running costs and increase scalability. PXN is proud to be backing Ismaeel and the team, who are tackling this head on.”
In one production deployment, Expanse identified nearly €6.9 million ($8 million) of idle compute capacity in a single month.
Expanse will use the funding to expand its engineering team, accelerate product development and bring its platform to more organisations across AI infrastructure, quantitative finance, life sciences, research and high performance computing.

articles.title: Canon's new EOS R8 Mark II hasn't reached the entry-level full-frame bar set by Nikon over a year ago — here's how it compares to the Z5 II
articles.text:
The year-old Nikon Z5 II is still streets ahead of Canon's new EOS R8 Mark II — and it's the entry-level full-frame camera I’d buy
Canon's new EOS R8 Mark II hasn't reached the bar set by Nikon over a year ago
Canon's EOS R8 Mark II is here, with a fresh new look that's inspired by the world's leading camera manufacturer's heritage, and finished off with a "modern twist". The resemblance to Canon's analog SLRs such as the T80 or AE-1 is faint, but in any case the new model is certainly a decent upgrade of the EOS R8, adding image stabilization, a multi-controller, and various performance and design improvements.
When I pored over the specs and pricing of the EOS R8 Mark II during my hands-on, however, a surprising reality came into sharp focus: Nikon's year-and-a-bit-old Z5 II remains highly competitive and it costs less than Canon's latest entry-level full-frame mirrorless model.
If you're considering your first full-frame camera and are not tied to Canon or another system, you should totally read on to find out more about the new EOS R8 Mark II, and how it fares against our Camera of the Year 2025 winner, the Nikon Z5 II.
1. Sensor
- Both feature a 24MP full-frame sensor
- Both sensors are equipped with image stabilization, rated up to 7.5EV
This section is going to be straightforward: both cameras have a full-frame 24MP sensor that's equipped with image stabilization (IBIS) rated up to 7.5EV.
Besides nuances in how each camera handles color and noise, and personal preferences, the image quality will be pretty similar. Having said that, I've historically found Canon's image stabilization to perform better than Nikon's.
- Sensor winner: Tie
2. Video
- Both shoot 4K video up to 60fps, but the Z5 II has a 1.5x crop
- Both shoot 4K 30fps with 10-bit color depth from the sensor's full width, the Z5 II shoots 12-bit RAW
- 1080p slow motion recording up to 180fps (EOS R8 Mark II) and 120fps (Nikon Z5 II)
- Color profiles for video; new 'filmtones' for EOS R8 II, well-regarded RED profiles for Z5 II
There's much more to unpack and compare regarding each camera's video features. Both can shoot 4K video at 30fps with 4:2:2 10-bit color depth from the full width of the sensor, and up to 60fps at this resolution, although at this frame rate there's a 1.5x crop in the Z5 II.
The Nikon camera, however, is the only one that can shoot 12-bit internal RAW video, which certainly gives it the quality edge for users who want greater tonal depth and editing latitude, and who don't mind the larger file sizes.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Slow motion recording is also possible in 1080p, but again the EOS R8 Mark II has the frame rates edge — it can shoot 6x slow motion (180fps) to the Z5 II's 4x slow motion (120fps).
There's no shortage of color profiles for each camera, either. There's each company's version of a gradable, flat Log profile (C Log and N-Log) and Rec 709, while Canon has introduced two new 'filmtones' looks and the Nikon Z5 II features a RED RAW profile. Each can link with a companion app to import custom profiles, too. Users with either camera should have no issues getting a style they like.
Both camera's video recording is supported by powerful autofocus and image stabilization, making smooth and sharp run-and-gun filming a distinct possibility. The EOS R8 Mark II features a tally lamp to indicate when recording is active, but the Z5 II offers dual SD card slots for overflow / backup storage, whereas the Canon camera just has the one slot.
There are distinct advantages for each camera — and more besides that I haven't got into here — and as such it's tricky to call an outright winner in this category.
- Video winner: Tie
3. Design
- Canon EOS R8 Mark II: 546g body (with battery and card), not weather resistant, single card slot
- Nikon Z5 II: 700g body (with battery and card), weather resistant mag alloy, dual card slot
The EOS R8 Mark II is the guinea pig for Canon's new design. It forgoes the sweeping curves we've come to associate with Canon camera, in favor of straight, angular lines and a pronounced viewfinder bump that are "inspired by Canon's heritage". In this sense, it actually has more in common with the Nikon camera than previous Canon models.
Beyond the looks, the cameras are roughly the same size, but the EOS R8 Mark II is notably lighter at 546g. The quality of its buttons, controls and body have a much more entry-level feel to them, whereas the Z5 II feels more like a level up. The Z5 II feels like the more robust of the two, plus it's officially noted as weather resistant whereas the EOS R8 Mark II is not. The gulf in quality is compounded by the displays...
- Design winner: Nikon Z5 II
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
4. Displays
- Canon EOS R8 Mark: 3.0-inch 1.62m-dot vari-angle LCD and 0.39-inch 2.36m-dot EVF
- Nikon Z5 II: 3.2-inch 2.1m-dot vari-angle LCD and 0.5-inch 3.69m-dot EVF
Put simply, the Nikon Z5 II's LCD screen and EVF displays are higher-specced than the EOS R8 Mark II's, despite the camera arriving almost 18 months earlier.
Both screens are vari-angle, so they can be pulled out to the side of the camera and tilted for low-level shooting / rotated for selfies. The Z5 II's display is slightly larger at 3.2-inches to the Canon's 3.0-inches, and it has a higher resolution, although the pixel density is roughly the same.
I've used both cameras separately, but can attest to the superior quality of the Z5 II's EVF – it's physically bigger, has more pixels, higher magnification, and is brighter — in short, a more immersive display. This category is an easy win for the Z5 II.
- Displays winner: Nikon Z5 II
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
5. Performance
- Canon EOS R8 Mark: 220-shot (VF) / 340-shot (LCD) battery life, Dual Pixel CMOS AF II, 40fps with pre-capture
- Nikon Z5 II: 340-shot (VF) / 350-shot (LCD) battery life, Hybrid phase detection AF, 30fps with pre-capture
If you prefer using a viewfinder, then the battery life of the Z5 II is much better than the EOS R8 Mark II, although the playing field is somewhat levelled when using the LCD. Neither camera has a particularly impressive battery life, but both can be recharged on the go, via USB-C.
Both also have excellent autofocus performance, with subject tracking and detection for humans, animals and vehicles. I haven't directly compared the performance of each camera, but they do inherit autofocus systems from pricier models that I have tested at length. Canon's 'Register People' mode is super handy for prioritizing specific people in crowded scenes — and you can store up to 10 faces at any one time.
Canon improved autofocus sensitivity in low light down to -7.5EV in its second-gen EOS R8, but the Nikon camera was already more sensitive, being rated to -10EV.
For outright burst shooting speeds, Canon has the edge — it's capable of up to 40fps, compared to 30fps for the Nikon. However, neither are true sports cameras in the sense that once the buffer is full, they will slow up quicker than high-end models. The Z5 II has both a mechanical and electronic shutter, while the Canon model only has the latter.
- Performance winner: Tie
6. Price and availability
- Canon EOS R8 Mark II announced on Sep 16, 2026, for $1,899 / £1,729 / AU$2,529
- Nikon Z5 II was released on April 3, 2025 for $1,699 / £1,599 / AU$2,699, but the price has since dropped
Canon's EOS R8 Mark II has only just been announced at the time of writing, and its sales start date is October 20. It will cost $1,899 / £1,729 / AU$2,529 body only, or £2,119.99 / AU$2,859 with the budget 24-105mm F4-7.1 kit lens / $2099 with the 24-50mm f/4.5-6.3 IS STM lens in the US. Naturally, there are no price cuts yet.
Nikon's Z5 II, meanwhile, was released almost 18 months ago, and at list price was approximately 10% cheaper in the US and UK, but a little more in Australia — so no huge difference. However, it has since come down in price, and that margin has increased. Like the Canon model, it's available in a kit with a 24-105mm F4-7.1 lens, but there are other good-value kits on sale, including with the 24-200mm travel zoom.
- Price winner: Nikon Z5 II
Canon EOS R8 Mark II vs Nikon Z5 II: early verdict
As entry-level full-frame cameras, the Canon EOS R8 Mark II and Nikon Z5 II share many key features, including things like a 24MP full-frame sensor with image stabilization, 4K video recording and powerful autofocus.
There are specific features unique to each model that stand out, but not enough to swing the balance either way. However, where the gulf becomes clear is in each camera's overall handling and quality — the Nikon Z5 II's superior displays, control layout, body quality, extra card slot and better battery life deliver a better all-round shooting experience.
The Canon feels every much the entry-level camera with powerful features, whereas the Nikon camera redefines entry-level quality. And when you think that the Z5 II has pricier components but costs less, it feels like a solid win for the Canon rival.

articles.title: Nvidia reportedly denies RTX 5090 warranty over faded serial number
articles.text:
Nvidia reportedly denies RTX 5090 warranty over faded serial number — $6,500 GPU blemish not an isolated incident, according to customers
The GeForce RTX 5090 is the first thing that comes to mind when you think of the best graphics cards. However, you'd better pray the serial number on the inside of the metal bracket does not fade over time, since that could be a reason for Nvidia to reject warranty claims. At least one Redditor has shared a case of Nvidia reportedly denying a warranty claim because the bracket's serial number was unreadable.
The Redditor Willing-Avocado-4830, based in the UK, began experiencing black-screen crashes with a GeForce RTX 5090 Founders Edition graphics card under heavy load. The user sent the card to Nvidia for a warranty claim. After 30 days of radio silence, the owner finally received an email stating that their RMA request was rejected with no apparent explanation for the denial.
Seeking clarification, the user reached out to Nvidia for further information. According to the Redditor's recount, Nvidia support purportedly rejected the RMA because the serial number on the graphics card's metal bracket had faded. Like many gamers, Willing-Avocado-4830 claims never to have modified or tampered with the graphics card after installation. The fading serial number does not appear to be an isolated incident. Several other owners have reported similar issues in the Reddit discussion.
The metal bracket on graphics cards is susceptible to dust buildup, oxidation, and corrosion over time. This can cause it to look dirty, stained, or sometimes slightly discolored compared to when it was brand new. These same phenomena could have affected the serial number's legibility, especially since it is printed with ink onto the bracket's surface rather than etched for better durability. For comparison, the last-generation GeForce RTX 4090 Founders Edition had its serial number laser-etched onto the metal bracket.
One Redditor said that someone in the Nvidia Discord channel recommended cleaning the area with isopropyl alcohol to restore the serial number's visibility. However, that may not work if the ink is no longer present, as previous reports suggest the hot air expelled by the Founders Edition cooler could be erasing the serial number.
Surprisingly, Nvidia rejected a warranty claim solely because of a faded serial number on the graphics card’s bracket. The same serial number is clearly printed on a sticker on Nvidia's modular PCIe connector, which the chipmaker's technicians can verify when disassembling the GeForce RTX 5090. Moreover, you can pull the serial number from the graphics card through the command prompt with Nvidia SMI (System Management Interface), assuming the card is still working, which, in this case, it is. Willing-Avocado-4830 still had the original packaging and the original invoice from Nvidia U.K., so it would be easy to cross-reference the serial numbers.
Redditor hawok reportedly sent their GeForce RTX 5090 Founders Edition for RMA two months ago and encountered a similar situation. The serial number on the metal bracket was only partially visible. However, customer support seemingly accepted the RMA after the user sent photographs of the packaging that corroborated the serial number. It is unclear what Nvidia's policy is, or whether the chipmaker handles each case differently. We have reached out to Nvidia for clarification.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Some Redditors have suggested taking a photograph that shows the graphics card's serial number next to the packaging's serial number. Others jokingly recommend putting a piece of tape over the serial number. It might not be a bad idea, but you would need heat-resistant tape, something like Kapton tape.
GeForce RTX 5090 stock has practically disappeared from the U.S. market, with very few units starting at $6,500, 3.25X over the Blackwell flagship's MSRP. You cannot blame GeForce RTX 5090 owners for worrying. They already have a lot on their plates, dealing with the 16-pin power connector melting woes, and now also have to worry about fading serial numbers.

articles.title: Meet a mouse whose brain cortex is made up of human cells
articles.text:
Meet a mouse whose brain cortex is made up of human cells
“Xenocortical mice” are a dramatic demonstration of organoid technologies
Multiple cameras tracked a mouse as it wandered around a small arena. A computer charted its position and speed, leaving Pong-like traces on a monitor.
The reason to watch this rodent so carefully? Nearly half its brain volume had been replaced with human cells.
The effort to mix the brain tissues of distant species is being reported today in the journal Nature by a team at Stanford University, led by neuroscientist Sergiu Pașca.
Pașca’s group previously showed that human brain “organoids”—small blobs of neural tissue—could survive, and even function, after being injected into the heads of baby rodents.
Now, Pașca has taken things a step further by genetically modifying mice so their brains don’t fully develop in the first place. These modified mice are missing most cells of both the cortex and the hippocampus, two key brain areas.
That creates much more room for the human cells to take hold, he says. “Human cells that are placed in these animals will divide, will grow, and within a few weeks to a few months they will take most of that space,” he says. Pașca says one surprising discovery is that the mice lacking brain tissue seemed fairly normal—they walked around and squeaked. But they did have memory problems. In a maze test, they couldn’t remember what parts they’d explored.
The mice with the added human cells, by contrast, performed better on the maze test. That means the human tissue is playing some role in the animals’ cognition.
Pașca believes what he is calling “xenocortical mice” could be useful in studying brain injuries. However, the report is also a dramatic demonstration of “the combined power of genetic engineering and stem-cell technology to reshape biology,” says Carsten Charlesworth, a scientist who works in a different Stanford lab and was not involved in the research.
Already, brain organoids are being tested in labs to see if they can be connected to computers to play video games. Other scientists have proposed using them like replacement parts to treat stroke victims.
“What’s most remarkable to me is the extent to which human neural tissue introduced after birth grew and connected with the mouse nervous system across a species barrier,” says Charlesworth. “As these technologies advance, they’ll increasingly force us to challenge our traditional assumptions.”
Last year, Pașca convened a group of ethics experts to study the implications of neural organoid technology, including the odds that an animal could develop human consciousness and the risk that “organoid therapy clinics” might offer scam treatments to desperate patients.
For now, he says, he’s not concerned that the rodents have any type of human cognitive capacities. That is because their brains are relatively tiny and the evolutionary distance between man and mouse is so great.
But that’s also why Pașca says this type of experiment should not be carried out on higher species: They could end up with large volumes of functioning human brain tissue, potentially blurring the cognitive boundaries between people and animals.
Pașca specifically cautioned against adding human brain organoids to a monkey engineered to lack a cortex.
“One of the things that I see as a very clear red line is doing this experiment in a primate,” he says. “I don’t think that is justified at this point in any way.”

articles.title: Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush
articles.text:
According to The Information, Apple is planning to get back into the server game and might just pair up with NVIDIA to make it happen. Apple retired its Xserve line in 2011 and has largely left enterprise machines to other manufacturers since. But the growing demand for compute power as the AI industry continues to expand has apparently led the company to believe there is an opening for its powerful but efficient ARM-based M processors. Its Mac Mini and Mac Studio have proven popular with AI developers, which has led to shortages.
Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush
The company could borrow tech from Nvidia to make it happen.
The server product, whether it’s called Xserve or something else, likely won’t debut until 2029. Word is that it will run on two or four (depending on the model) M8 Ultra chips. Apple only just announced the M6 in August, so the M8 line is a ways out.
It’s also rumored that Apple’s servers could incorporate Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion tech, which connects multiple chips together so they can operate as one. While the two companies have historically had a frosty relationship behind the scenes, recently Apple turned to Nvidia chips to power its revamped Siri servers. Incorporating NVLink could lead to further collaboration between the two, but plans could still change.

articles.title: SK Hynix reportedly in talks with Intel to build memory chips in US | TechCrunch
articles.text:
South Korean memory chip giant SK Hynix is in discussions with Intel to manufacture RAM chips in the U.S. for the first time, Reuters reported, citing anonymous sources.
The companies have reportedly discussed various options, one of which would have SK Hynix leasing space at Intel’s planned factory in Ohio to manufacture the chips. The chipmakers are also said to be considering a joint venture that could include cloud-service providers.
SK Hynix told TechCrunch on Wednesday that nothing has been finalized yet. “SK Hynix is exploring various options to strengthen its global competitiveness, but no specific plans or arrangements have been finalized at this time,” the Korean semiconductor company said in a statement. “No decisions have been made regarding the two scenarios mentioned in the article.”
The Korean chip giant, which has benefited massively from skyrocketing demand for high-bandwidth memory RAM chips used in data centers for AI applications, is already building a $3.8 billion advanced packaging and research facility for AI chips in West Lafayette, Indiana, with mass production expected to begin in 2029. The factory will use DRAM wafers made in South Korea and package them into HBM chips.
It remains unclear what types of memory chips the company would produce in Ohio if the deal goes through.
As a global chip shortage worsens, the Trump administration is seeking to expand production on American soil. The White House said in January that it could impose broader tariffs on semiconductor imports while offering tariff relief to companies investing in domestic manufacturing.
SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won signaled support for U.S. chip production in July, saying the company should build factories in the U.S., if feasible, alongside those in South Korea’s Honam region. That month, the chipmaker listed its American depository receipts on the Nasdaq, broadening its access to American investors.
The potential deal with Intel could face scrutiny at home. Seoul holds that the decision would be up to SK Hynix, but any plan involving strategically important chip technology could trigger a government review under a law designed to prevent sensitive technology from being transferred overseas, according to Reuters.
Intel and SK Hynix have done business before: In 2020, Intel sold its NAND flash-memory business to SK Hynix for $9 billion.
Intel did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment outside regular business hours.

articles.title: GTA-Nostalgie: 9 Dinge, die nur Gamer der 90er und 2000er kennen
articles.text:
GTA-Nostalgie: 9 Dinge, die nur Gamer der 90er und 2000er kennen
Es passiert tatsächlich noch: Am 19. November soll Grand Theft Auto 6 endlich erscheinen, nachdem das Spiel mehrere Male verschoben wurde. Ganze 13 Jahre nachdem der Vorgänger GTA 5 erstmals für die Playstation 3 und Xbox 360 erschienen ist. Das Spiel dürfte das teuerste in der bisherigen Geschichte der Videospiele sein. Und gleichzeitig in der ersten Woche so viel Geld einspielen wie noch kein anderes Spiel zuvor.
Die GTA-Serie ist spätestens seit dem dritten Teil bekannt dafür, neue Standards zu setzen. Sei es in der Weitläufigkeit von offenen Spielwelten und in der Anzahl an Ingame-Radiostationen, die reale Songs abspielen, während man im Auto durch die lebendigen Straßen fährt.
Dabei sind in den vergangenen Jahrzehnten einige Momente entstanden, die vielen Gamern noch in Erinnerung sein dürften – besonders jenen, die schon seit den 90er Jahren Fans von Grand Theft Auto sind. Einige dieser Momente haben wir zusammengetragen.

articles.title: Mira el grandioso nuevo tráiler de 'Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha', el regreso más espectacular a Panem
articles.text:
La próxima película de Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha acaba de lanzar su asombroso nuevo tráiler. Un adelanto con el que la película prepara a sus fans para lo que está por venir. Porque esta no es solo una historia más dentro del universo distópico de la saga. Es, en realidad, uno de los relatos más crudos e intensos de toda la franquicia. El regreso a Panem está más cerca que nunca y el avance deja claro que no se van a guardar nada.
Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha es precuela de la saga original nos remonta veinticuatro años atrás en el tiempo. Allí conoceremos la historia pasada de Haymitch Abernathy, quien más adelante fuera mentor de Katniss Everdeen y Peeta Melark. El joven Haymitch deberá acatar las normas del presidente Snow y luchar por su vida en la arena.
Y es que lo que se celebra en Panem es la 50º edición de los Juegos del Hambre, también denominados como el Segundo Vasallaje de los Veinticinco. Como tributo del Distrito 12, el protagonista participa en el tradicional espectáculo que tanto fascina a los habitantes del Capitolio. Las pruebas, como vemos en el tráiler de Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha, serán más despiadadas que nunca. Sin embargo, la llama de la rebelión está a punto de cambiar los juegos para siempre.
Mira el tráiler de Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha
Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha cuenta con un reparto estelar conformado por Joseph Zada como Haymitch Abernathy, Ralph Fiennes como el presidente Snow, Jesse Plemons como Plutarch Heavensbee, Glenn Close como Drusilla Sickle, Elle Faning como Effie Trinket o Whitney Peak como Lenore Dove Baird o Kieran Culkin como el presentador Caesar Flickerman.
Junto a ellos, otros nombres de la talla de Maya Hawke como Wiress, Mckenna Grace como Maysilee Donner, Kelvin Harrison Jr. como Beetee, Lili Taylor como Mags, Ben Wang como Wyatt y las niñas Molly McCann e Iona Bell como Louella y Lou Lou. Además, está confirmado el regreso, probablemente en forma de cameo en un flashforward, de Jennifer Lawrence y Josh Hutcherson como Katniss Everdeen y Peeta Melark.
Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha, adaptación del libro homónimo de la escritora Suzanne Collins, se estrena en cines el 20 de noviembre.

articles.title: Meta dévoile de nouveaux abonnements payants pour Instagram, WhatsApp et Facebook
articles.text:
Si Meta a toujours assuré que ses services resteront gratuits, l’entreprise n’hésite pas depuis un certain temps maintenant à proposer des abonnements payants, pour échapper à la publicité ou pour bénéficier de fonctionnalités exclusives. Justement, Meta vient d’annoncer une mise à niveau de ses abonnements Meta One. Les abonnements Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus et Facebook Plus ont ainsi été enrichis de nouvelles fonctionnalités. Nous comptons aussi deux nouvelles offres pour les particuliers et quatre nouveaux abonnements à destination des professionnels.
Meta enrichit ses offres Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus et Facebook Plus
Les offres Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus et Facebook Plus ont été lancées en juin dernier. Elles sont aujourd’hui enrichies de nouvelles fonctionnalités. Instagram Plus permet désormais d’ajouter des polices personnalisées dans les messages privés et les Stories, d’envoyer des notifications lorsque certaines personnes consultent votre Story et d’afficher des aperçus des messages privés.
De son côté, Facebook Plus ajoute des options de personnalisation pour Messenger, offre davantage d’informations sur les Reels et étend les super réactions aux Reels et aux publications du fil d’actualité. Enfin, WhatsApp Plus testera prochainement deux nouvelles fonctionnalités : le stockage des sauvegardes de conversations et de médias, ainsi que les planifications de groupe. Ces dernières permettent de mettre en sourdine ou de masquer certaines discussions selon un horaire défini, afin d’être plus tranquille. Instagram Plus et Facebook Plus sont facturés 2,99 € par mois, contre 2,49 € par mois pour WhatsApp Plus. À noter que certaines de ces nouvelles fonctionnalités seront étendues aux lunettes connectées de l’entreprise.
Deux nouvelles offres : Meta One Core et Meta One Premium
Meta One Core, facturé 7,99 dollars par mois, propose la création et l’édition d’images ainsi que la génération de vidéos à l’aide des modèles Muse, une utilisation plus fréquente des outils d’IA intégrés aux applications, comme Restyle sur Instagram, ainsi que des effets vocaux sur Instagram. En d’autres termes, il est ici question d’une production de contenu multimédia plus poussée grâce à Meta AI. Cet abonnement intègre par ailleurs les fonctionnalités d’Instagram Plus, de Facebook Plus et de WhatsApp Plus.
Meta One Premium, facturé 19,99 dollars par mois, offre les mêmes fonctionnalités, mais avec une capacité de calcul plus importante pour les requêtes complexes et davantage de possibilités de génération d’images et de vidéos.
Quatre nouveaux abonnements pour les professionnels
Nous comptons au total quatre nouveaux abonnements destinés aux professionnels : Meta One Essentiel (14,99 $/mois), Meta One Advanced (49,99 $/mois), Meta One Expert (149 $/mois) et Meta One Max (499 $/mois). Ces quatre abonnements offrent aux créateurs et aux entreprises un niveau d’accès aux outils variable selon l’offre choisie, pour mettre en œuvre leurs campagnes de communication sur les réseaux sociaux de Meta.
À titre d’exemple, l’offre Essentiel donne un accès étendu à Meta Business Agent sur WhatsApp « pour répondre à vos clients 24h/24 et 7j/7 », tandis que les offres One Expert et One Max incluent « un accès optimal aux fonctionnalités et une capacité maximale d’agent métier Meta pour les équipes gérant des projets de grande envergure ». Enfin, Meta assure que l’expérience de base de ses applications et de Meta AI a toujours été gratuite et que cela ne changera pas.

articles.title: Android 17 QPR1 arrive : voici les nouveautés majeures de ce déploiement stable
articles.text:
On l’attendait, la voici enfin : Android 17 QPR1 est parmi nous. Cette mise à jour, qui fait suite à de nombreuses versions bêta, comprend plusieurs nouveautés intéressantes.
Android 17 se perfectionne, malgré quelques bugs recensés par les utilisateurs : Google a renforcé la sécurité du code de déverrouillage, favorisé l’accès à un son haute résolution via le Bluetooth, imposé des limites de mémoire aux applications pour optimiser les performances des smartphones et bien plus encore.
Bonne nouvelle, une première mise à jour stable d’Android 17 vient de pointer le bout de son nez. Et le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que les équipes de Google étaient inspirées. On fait le point.
Une interface modernisée
Mishaal Rahman, responsable de l’engagement communautaire pour Android, vient d’annoncer, dans un post publié sur Reddit, l’arrivée d’Android 17 QPR1. Cette mise à jour inclut pas mal de nouveautés qui devraient beaucoup plaire aux utilisateurs.
Google a, dans un premier temps, concentré ses efforts sur le design de son système d’exploitation mobile :
- Des effets de flou ont été ajoutés un peu partout, du menu contextuel de l’écran d’accueil aux dossiers d’applications, en passant par le panneau de volume ;
- L’icône des paramètres Android et le menu contextuel de l’écran d’accueil ont eu droit à un relooking ;
- Les réglages rapides sont devenus plus dynamiques avec l’inclusion de nouvelles animations et d’aperçus de retour prédictifs ;
- Le carrousel multimédia a aussi été modernisé : un petit aperçu de la carte suivante est désormais visible sur sa droite et il est possible de glisser plus facilement d’une session à une autre. Quant au bouton de sélection de sortie audio, son design a également été entièrement revu.
Google pense aussi à votre bien-être numérique : l’option « Pause Point », annoncée lors du dernier évènement I/O, fait, en effet, partie de la mise à jour. Cette fonctionnalité intègre un bref délai avant l’ouverture d’une application un peu trop distrayante. Cela suffira-t-il à dissuader les utilisateurs d’aller plus loin ? Rien n’est moins sûr…
Côté personnalisation, il est désormais possible de jongler entre plusieurs écrans de veille mais aussi de paramétrer le motif de vibration de chaque sonnerie. Ceux qui utilisent le terminal Linux embarqué auront aussi la joie de pouvoir personnaliser leurs polices, couleurs et raccourcis clavier.
De nombreuses évolutions du côté de la productivité
Les équipes de Google ont trouvé quelques belles idées pour booster la productivité des utilisateurs :
- Sur les grands écrans, la barre des tâches met en avant les applis récemment ouvertes au lieu des suggestions algorithmiques autrefois disponibles ;
- Le mode Bureau gagne en flexibilité grâce à des raccourcis apparaissant au survol et à des fenêtres PiP libres ;
- Il est aussi possible de glisser-déposer le contenu d’une bulle vers une autre fenêtre.
On note également l’arrivée d’une nouvelle vignette dans les Paramètres Rapides qui permet de lancer votre application de prise de notes préférée. Un raccourci additionnel a notamment été prévu dans un coin de l’écran pour les possesseurs de souris ou de trackpad.
Des améliorations pour la confidentialité et la sécurité
Du côté de la confidentialité, Google a intégré deux nouveautés :
- Au lieu de filmer tout ce qui s’affiche, l’enregistreur d’écran se concentre désormais sur l’application utilisée au moment du lancement de l’enregistrement. Pas de panique cependant, il est possible d’élargir le cadre de façon manuelle ;
- Grâce à une nouvelle API, les applications peuvent demander la permission de conserver les informations de localisation incluses dans les photos qui leur sont envoyées.
Google n’oublie pas non plus la sécurité : une toute nouvelle fonction de vérification du système a fait son apparition dans les paramètres. Elle permet notamment de contrôler l’authenticité des builds installés, et permet, si on le souhaite, d’utiliser un second appareil pour vérifier les informations, via un QR Code.
Les téléphones Pixel en première ligne
Au-delà de ça, d’autres ajustements mineurs complètent le tableau : le globe qui permet de changer de clavier peut être masqué dans la barre de navigation, le réglage de l’heure propose désormais 3 modes clairs (automatique, 12h et 24h) et l’outil Health Connect peut se baser sur les données du podomètre de votre téléphone pour calculer les distances parcourues et les calories perdues. Conformément aux demandes des utilisateurs, une nouvelle option permet également de couper l’avertissement qui s’affiche lorsqu’on active les données mobiles.
On le voit, même s’il n’y a rien de révolutionnaire, Google était tout de même d’humeur généreuse. Comme d’habitude, les propriétaires de Pixel seront les premiers à pouvoir profiter d’Android 17 QPR1 et les autres constructeurs devront prendre leur mal en patience avant d’y avoir accès. Notez que Google prévoit d’ores et déjà une nouvelle mise à jour trimestrielle, qui devrait arriver d’ici la fin de l’année.

articles.title: 275 km d'altitude, 10 heures de mission et 6 tours de la Terre : ce que vise la fusée géante Starship pour son vol orbital inédit
articles.text:
On connaissait l’objectif général, mais on ignorait le programme en détail : depuis des mois, SpaceX prépare son tout premier vol orbital avec la fusée géante Starship, dont le développement se poursuit. Un vol attendu à partir du 22 septembre 2026, sous réserve des feux verts réglementaires, qui suit les treize lancements suborbitaux déjà menés.
À quelques jours du tir, on en sait désormais beaucoup plus. Une fois dans l’espace, le vaisseau (le « Ship », c’est-à-dire l’étage supérieur du lanceur) doit se stabiliser environ à 275 kilomètres d’altitude, soit presque à mi-chemin entre la Station spatiale internationale (ISS), qui tourne autour de 400 km, et le début de l’espace, fixé officiellement à 100 kilomètres.
Que va-t-il se passer pour le Starship une fois en orbite ?
À cette hauteur, il est prévu d’enchaîner six orbites autour de la Terre pour un vol qui doit durer près de dix heures. L’amerrissage doit advenir dans l’océan Pacifique, à l’ouest du Chili, à des milliers de kilomètres du point de départ texan. C’est un changement notable : le point de chute classique se faisait jusqu’alors dans l’océan Indien, au large de l’Australie.
Le vaisseau ne partira pas à vide. SpaceX prévoit de larguer 26 satellites Starlink V3, la dernière génération de son réseau d’accès à Internet, pour la première fois sur une orbite stable. Lors du 13e vol, le 24 juillet, l’entreprise avait certes déjà déployé 20 satellites Starlink V3, mais sur une trajectoire suborbitale de courte durée, sans les maintenir en service.
Chaque satellite V3 doit ajouter environ 1 térabit par seconde de capacité, soit 26 térabits au total sur ce seul vol, l’équivalent d’une dizaine de lancements de l’ancienne génération sur une Falcon 9. De quoi gonfler nettement les débits déjà performants d’un réseau qui aligne plus de 11 000 engins en orbite basse.
L’endurance du Starship durant cette mission sera évidemment scrutée de près. Jusqu’ici, les treize vols d’essai du lanceur se sont tous arrêtés à un saut suborbital, après avoir franchi plusieurs milliers de km. La fusée géante grimpait, filait le long d’une portion du globe, puis retombait sans jamais boucler un tour complet de la Terre.
Toute la difficulté est dans la descente
Mais il y a un autre moment qui sera observé avec une vive attention : la redescente vers la Terre, une séquence plus ardue que la montée. SpaceX précise d’ailleurs qu’il ne lancera la manœuvre d’insertion en orbite qu’après avoir vérifié qu’il reste assez de redondance sur le matériel nécessaire au retour. Il y a donc encore une incertitude.
Après ses nombreux tours de la Terre, le Starship devra rallumer un seul moteur Raptor pour freiner et quitter son orbite, une manœuvre de désorbitation que l’entreprise a testée cet été. Viendra ensuite la rentrée atmosphérique, là où le bouclier thermique a longtemps été présenté comme l’obstacle numéro un du programme.
Cette protection ne serait plus fondamentalement un problème, selon Elon Musk.
Quant au propulseur Super Heavy, il est prévu un amerrissage contrôlé au large, dans le golfe du Mexique. Il n’y aura pas de tentative de rattrapage du lanceur avec les bras mécaniques de la tour Mechazilla. Cette étape, elle aussi très attendue, pourrait advenir d’ici la fin de l’année, sauf péripétie qui paralyserait durablement Starbase.
L’amerrissage du Super Heavy est une manœuvre en théorie bien maîtrisée par SpaceX, mais elle n’est pas pour autant acquise à chaque fois : lors du 13e vol, il y avait eu un problème sur trois moteurs. Seuls dix moteurs sur les treize s’étaient rallumés, provoquant un amerrissage brutal. Mais SpaceX a assuré que des améliorations ont été apportées depuis.

articles.title: AIUC Raises $40 Million to Certify Enterprise AI Agents
articles.text:
AIUC (Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company) has announced raising $40 million in a Series A funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $55 million.
The investment round was led by Ribbit Capital, with additional support from First Harmonic.
Founded in 2024, San Francisco-based AIUC developed AIUC-1, an evaluation and risk standard designed to assess enterprise AI agents.
The standard checks AI agents against common risks, including jailbreaks, hallucinations, prompt injections, anomalous behavior, and data leaks.
The framework subjects AI models to roughly 5,000 adversarial risk scenarios, backed by quarterly audits to address emerging threat vectors.
The AIUC-1 standard, the startup says, is already used to certify some of the most popular AI agents, including Cursor, ElevenLabs, Fin, Harvey, KPMG, Lovable, and UiPath.
AIUC will use the new investment to expand its audits, standards, and insurance to frontier models.
“Most enterprises have a list of AI agents that were approved in pilots but stalled at the security review. Evidence of security and reliability is now the main bottleneck,” said AIUC founder Rune Kvist, who was Anthropic’s first product hire.

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass : fin du « Day 1 », multi en kit… Microsoft préparerait une refonte radicale
articles.text:
Parmi les services de cloud gaming, le Xbox Game Pass a connu pas mal de chamboulements ces derniers temps. Augmentations de prix successives, retour en arrière avec une baisse des tarifs, introduction de limites de temps de jeu… Et ce n’est visiblement pas terminé.
Sur les forums de Resetera, un leaker réputé fiable dit savoir ce que prépare Microsoft pour le Xbox Game Pass. En résumé, il ne ressemblerait plus à ce que l’on connaît aujourd’hui, découpant l’ensemble de ses fonctionnalités pour les proposer indépendamment les unes des autres.
Pourquoi payer la nouvelle génération au prix fort ? iPhone 17, iPhone 16 Pro et iPhone 15 Pro : trouvez le modèle parfait, révisé par des experts et garanti sur Back Market.
Le Xbox Game Pass pourrait être remanié en profondeur
Nous allons parler au présent, mais souvenez-vous de prendre les informations qui suivent au conditionnel. Le Xbox Game Pass « nouvelle formule » propose deux abonnements seulement : un avec publicité, comme celui disponible depuis juillet 2026, et un autre sans.
Celui avec réclame coûtera 12,99 dollars par mois, l’autre 19,99 dollars mensuels ou 239,99 dollars pour un an avec un seul paiement. Notez l’incohérence ici : c’est 0,11 dollar de plus que si vous payez chaque mois.
Viennent ensuite les options. Le cloud gaming, actuellement intégré dans les différentes formules, demande de débourser 5,99 dollars de plus chaque mois, pour 25 heures de jeu. Vous voulez du multijoueurs en ligne ? 10,99 dollars de plus sur la facture mensuelle. Idem pour un Plan Famille : 5,99 dollars.
Le dernier (gros) changement concerne la disparition des jeux disponibles sur le Xbox Game Pass dès leur sortie. Elle est compensée par une baisse du tarif mensuel de 3 dollars. Soit une maigre économie annuelle de 36 dollars au détriment de l’un des principaux intérêts du service de cloud gaming. Étrange. La fin des jeux « day 1 » démarrera entre février et avril 2027.
« Aucun changement à annoncer » pour Microsoft
Un porte-parole de Microsoft s’est exprimé sur ces rumeurs : « Nous testons régulièrement différentes offres Game Pass et examinons ce qui fonctionne le mieux pour les joueurs sur les différents marchés. Nous n’avons aucun changement à annoncer aujourd’hui ni de projets finalisés. »
La firme ajoute qu’« aucun changement n’est prévu concernant les jeux dont l’arrivée dans le Game Pass Ultimate dès leur sortie a déjà été annoncée ». Cela comprend une vingtaine de titres jusqu’en 2027, dont le prochain Fable. Au final, on ne peut pas vraiment parler de démenti formel. Cela laisse penser que la fuite a au moins un fond de vérité.
